translations.literal: Kang Baoyi, Ma Sui, Dong Yuanheng, Cao Jin, Kong Zongdan, Zhao Shidan, Su Jian, Qin Chuanxu, Zhan Liangchen, Jiang Zhongming, Li Ruoshui, Liu Ge, Fu Cha, Yang Zhen and his son Zongmin, Zhang Kejian, Zhang Que, Zhu Zhao, Shi Kang, Sun Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Baoyi, Ma Sui, Dong Yuanheng, Cao Jin, Kong Zongdan, Zhao Shidan, Su Jian, Qin Chuanxu, Zhan Liangchen, Jiang Zhongming, Li Ruoshui, Liu Ge, Fu Cha, Yang Zhen and his son Zongmin, Zhang Kejian, Zhang Que, Zhu Zhao, Shi Kang, and Sun Yi.

sentences.zh: 士大夫忠義之氣，至於五季，變化殆盡。

translations.literal: The spirit of loyalty and righteousness among scholar-officials, by the time of the Five Dynasties, had almost entirely changed and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties period, the scholar-official class's spirit of loyalty and righteousness had all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 宋之初興，范質、王溥，猶有餘憾，況其他哉！

translations.literal: At the beginning rise of Song, Fan Zhi and Wang Pu still had remaining regrets, how much more so the others!
translations.idiomatic: Even at the dawn of the Song, men such as Fan Zhi and Wang Pu still fell short of the ideal—what then of lesser men?

sentences.zh: 藝祖首褒韓通，次表衛融，足示意向。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor first praised Han Tong, then enshrined Wei Rong, sufficient to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor first honored Han Tong and then enshrined Wei Rong—acts that made his values plain enough.

sentences.zh: 厥後西北疆場之臣，勇於死敵，往往無懼。

translations.literal: Thereafter the ministers on the northwestern frontier, brave in facing death against the enemy, were often without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, officials on the northwestern frontier often showed no fear in dying against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 真、仁之世，田錫、王禹偁、范仲淹、歐陽修、唐介諸賢，以直言讜論倡於朝，於是中外搢紳知以名節相高，廉恥相尚，盡去五季之陋矣。

translations.literal: In the eras of Zhenzong and Renzong, worthy men such as Tian Xi, Wang Yucheng, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, and Tang Jie, with forthright speech and loyal remonstrance, took the lead at court; then within and without, gentry and officials knew to esteem one another for reputation and integrity, to value honor and shame, and completely cast off the vulgarity of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Zhenzong and Renzong, worthies such as Tian Xi, Wang Yucheng, Fan Zhongyan, Ouyang Xiu, and Tang Jie led the court with blunt, loyal counsel. Officials at home and abroad then came to measure one another by reputation and integrity, and the coarseness of the Five Dynasties was left behind.

sentences.zh: 故靖康之變，志士投袂，起而勤王，臨難不屈，所在有之。

translations.literal: Therefore at the Jingkang crisis, men of resolve shook their sleeves, rose to aid the throne, and faced hardship without yielding—such men were found everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Thus at the Jingkang crisis, resolute men rose up to rescue the throne, refusing to yield in the face of disaster—examples could be found everywhere.

sentences.zh: 及宋之亡，忠節相望，班班可書，匡直輔翼之功，蓋非一日之積也。

translations.literal: When Song perished, loyal integrity stood one after another, clearly recordable in writing; the achievement of rectifying and supporting the state was surely not accumulated in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Song fell, acts of loyal integrity stood in such profusion that they fill the records—virtue that had been building for generations, not forged overnight.

sentences.zh: 奉詔修三史，集儒臣議凡例，前代忠義之士，咸得直書而無諱焉。

translations.literal: By imperial order to compile the Three Histories, scholar-officials were gathered to discuss precedents; loyal and righteous men of former ages were all to be recorded straightforwardly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the Three Histories, we gathered scholar-officials to set the rules: loyal and righteous men of earlier ages were to be recorded plainly, without concealment.

sentences.zh: 然死節、死事，宜有別矣：若敵王所愾，勇往無前，或銜命出疆，或授職守土，或寓官閒居，感激赴義，雖所處不同，論其捐軀徇節，之死靡二，則皆為忠義之上者也；

translations.literal: Yet dying for integrity and dying in service ought to be distinguished: if one faces the king's foe with wrath, advances bravely without retreat, or bears imperial orders beyond the border, or receives office to guard the land, or holds a nominal post while living in retirement yet is moved to answer the call of righteousness—though their situations differ, in giving their bodies and following their principles unto death without duality, all belong among the highest of the loyal and righteous;
translations.idiomatic: Yet dying for principle and dying in official duty should be distinguished. Those who face the sovereign's enemy without flinching, who go forth on imperial mission abroad, who hold territorial office, or who live in retirement yet rush to duty when moved—all differ in circumstance, yet in giving their lives for principle without wavering they rank among the highest exemplars of loyalty and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 若勝負不常，陷身俘獲，或慷慨就死，或審義自裁，斯為次矣；

translations.literal: If victory and defeat are uncertain, one falls captive, yet either dies boldly or, discerning righteousness, takes one's own life—such belong to the next rank;
translations.idiomatic: Those whose fortunes waver, who fall captive yet die boldly or, judging what is right, take their own lives, belong to the next rank;

sentences.zh: 若蒼黃遇難，霣命亂兵，雖疑傷勇，終異苟免，況于國破家亡，主辱臣死，功雖無成，志有足尚者乎！

translations.literal: If in sudden peril one meets disaster and loses life to disorderly troops—though it may seem to impair courage, it is still unlike cowardly escape; how much more when state is broken and family destroyed, sovereign shamed and minister dies: though achievement is unfulfilled, is not the will still worthy of esteem!
translations.idiomatic: Those who perish suddenly amid chaos, though their deaths may seem less glorious, still differ from cowardly survival; and when the state falls and the sovereign is shamed, ministers who die though they cannot save the realm still deserve honor for their intent.

sentences.zh: 若夫世變淪胥，毀跡冥遁，能以貞厲保厥初心，抑又其次歟！

translations.literal: As for when the age changes and sinks together, one erases one's traces and withdraws in obscurity yet can by steadfast integrity preserve one's original heart—that is perhaps still a lower rank!
translations.idiomatic: When the age collapses and men efface themselves in hidden withdrawal, those who preserve their original integrity through steadfast resolve rank lower still.

sentences.zh: 至於布衣危言，嬰鱗觸諱，志在衛國，遑恤厥躬，及夫鄉曲之英，方外之傑，賈勇蹈義，厥死惟鈞。

translations.literal: As for commoners who speak dangerous words, brush scales and touch taboos, intent on guarding the state with no leisure to spare their persons; and local heroes, outstanding men beyond office, who sell their courage and tread righteousness—their deaths are equally weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who speak perilous truth, local heroes, and men outside official ranks who throw themselves into righteous action—their deaths, too, are weighed on the same scale when their aim is to serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 以類附從，定為等差，作《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: By category they are grouped and ranked in grades, composing the 'Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: Grouped by kind and ranked in order, we compose the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 康保裔

translations.literal: Kang Baoyi
translations.idiomatic: Kang Baoyi

sentences.zh: 契丹兵大入，諸將與戰於河間，保裔選精銳赴之，會暮，約詰朝合戰。

translations.literal: Khitan troops invaded in force; the generals fought them at Hejian. Baoyi selected elite troops and hastened there; night fell, and they agreed to join battle at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan army invaded in strength, the generals engaged them at Hejian. Baoyi led picked troops to the field; dusk fell, and they agreed to fight at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 遲明，契丹圍之數重，左右勸易甲馳突以出，保裔曰：「臨難無苟免。」

translations.literal: At first light the Khitan surrounded them in many rings; those beside him urged changing armor and charging out to escape. Baoyi said: 'In hardship there is no cowardly escape.'
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Khitan had surrounded them in layer after layer. His attendants urged him to change armor and break out, but Baoyi said, "In peril one must not seek a coward's escape."

sentences.zh: 遂決戰。

translations.literal: He then resolved on battle.
translations.idiomatic: With that he gave battle.

sentences.zh: 二日，殺傷甚眾，蹴踐塵深二尺，兵盡矢絕，援不至，遂沒焉。

translations.literal: For two days the killing and wounding were very many; trampled dust stood two feet deep; troops were exhausted and arrows spent; reinforcements did not arrive; he perished there.
translations.idiomatic: For two days the slaughter was immense, and trampled dust rose two feet deep. When his men and arrows were spent and no aid came, he fell.

sentences.zh: 時車駕駐大名，聞之震悼，廢朝二日，贈侍中。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was stationed at Daming; on hearing this he was shaken and grieved, suspended court for two days, and posthumously granted him Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Daming. Shocked and grieved, he suspended court for two days and posthumously made Baoyi Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 以其子繼英為六宅使、順州刺史，繼彬為洛苑使，繼明為內園副使，幼子繼宗為西頭供奉官，孫惟一為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: His son Jiying was made Commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Shunzhou; Jibin was made Luoyuan Commissioner; Jiming was made Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Parks; his youngest son Jizong was made Western Head Attendant-in-Attendance; his grandson Weiyi was made Master of Records in the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiying was appointed Commissioner of the Six Residences and prefect of Shunzhou; Jibin became Luoyuan Commissioner; Jiming, Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Parks; his youngest son Jizong, Western Head Attendant-in-Attendance; and his grandson Weiyi, master of records in the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 繼英等奉告命，謝曰：「臣父不能決勝而死，陛下不以罪其孥幸矣，臣等顧蒙非常之恩！」

translations.literal: Jiying and the others received the edict and thanked him, saying: 'Our father could not win victory and died; Your Majesty does not punish his children—that is already fortunate; how can we look to receive extraordinary favor!'
translations.idiomatic: Jiying and his brothers received the edict and said, "Our father died without victory; that Your Majesty does not punish his family is mercy enough—how can we accept such extraordinary favor?"

sentences.zh: 因悲涕伏地不能起。

translations.literal: They then wept in grief, prostrated on the ground, and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and prostrated themselves, unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 上惻然曰：「爾父死王事，贈賞之典，所宜加厚。」

translations.literal: The emperor said compassionately: 'Your father died in the king's service; the rites of posthumous reward ought to be made heavier.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with compassion, "Your father died in the state's service; his rewards should be all the greater."

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「保裔父、祖死疆場，身復戰沒，世有忠節，深可嘉也。」

translations.literal: He turned and said to those beside him: 'Baoyi's father and grandfather died on the frontier, and he too perished in battle; loyalty through generations—deeply admirable.'
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants he said, "Baoyi's father and grandfather died on the frontier, and he too fell in battle—a house of loyalty across generations, truly admirable."

sentences.zh: 保裔有母年八十四，遣使勞問，賜白金五十兩，封為陳國太夫人，其妻已亡，亦追封河東郡夫人。

translations.literal: Baoyi had a mother aged eighty-four; he sent envoys to console her, granted fifty taels of white gold, and enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Chen; his wife was already dead and was also posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi's mother was eighty-four; the emperor sent envoys to console her, gave fifty taels of silver, and enfeoffed her as Grand Lady of Chen. His deceased wife was posthumously made Lady of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 保裔謹厚好禮，喜賓客，善騎謝，弋飛走無不中。

translations.literal: Baoyi was careful, sincere, and fond of ritual; he delighted in guests; he was skilled at riding and archery; in hunting flying and running game he never missed.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyi was careful, courteous, and hospitable, skilled in riding and archery; in the hunt he never missed bird or beast.

sentences.zh: 嘗握矢三十，引滿以射，筈鏑相連而墜，人服其妙。

translations.literal: Once he grasped thirty arrows, drew to the full and shot; nock and point linked together as they fell, and people admired his skill.
translations.idiomatic: Once he shot thirty arrows in succession, each striking the last so that they fell linked together—a feat men marveled at.

sentences.zh: 屢經戰陣，身被七十創。

translations.literal: He passed through battle lines many times and bore seventy wounds on his body.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in many battles and bore seventy wounds.

sentences.zh: 貸公錢數十萬勞軍，沒後，親吏鬻器玩以償，上知之，乃復厚賜焉。

translations.literal: He borrowed several hundred thousand in public funds to reward the troops; after his death his personal clerks sold vessels and curios to repay; the emperor learned of it and again bestowed generously.
translations.idiomatic: He had borrowed hundreds of thousands in public funds to reward his troops. After his death his clerks sold his valuables to repay the debt; when the emperor learned of this, he bestowed further gifts.

sentences.zh: 繼英仕至左衛大將軍、貴州團練使，嚴於馭軍，厚於撫宗族，其卒也，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Jiying rose in office to General of the Left Guard and regimental commander of Guizhou; he was strict in commanding troops and generous in caring for his clan; when he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying rose to General of the Left Guard and regimental commander of Guizhou, strict with his troops but generous to his kin; he died leaving no wealth behind.

sentences.zh: 方保裔及契丹血戰，而援兵不至，惟張凝以高陽關路鈴轄領先鋒，李重貴以高陽關行營副都部署率眾策應，遇契丹兵交戰，保裔為敵所覆，重貴與凝赴援，腹背受敵，自申至寅力戰，敵乃退。

translations.literal: While Baoyi was locked in bloody battle with the Khitan and reinforcements did not arrive, only Zhang Ning as frontier commissioner of Gaoyang Pass led the vanguard, and Li Chonggui as deputy commander of the Gaoyang Pass field headquarters led troops in support; they met Khitan forces in battle. Baoyi was overrun by the enemy; Chonggui and Ning rushed to aid, attacked front and rear, fought fiercely from the shen hour to the yin hour, and the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyi fought the Khitan to the death and no reinforcements came, Zhang Ning of Gaoyang Pass led the vanguard and Li Chonggui the supporting force. When Baoyi was overrun, Chonggui and Ning came to his aid, fought with enemies before and behind from mid-afternoon until dawn, and drove the Khitan back.

sentences.zh: 當時諸將多失部分，獨重貴、凝全軍還屯，凝議上將士功狀，重貴喟然曰：「大將陷沒，而吾曹計功，何面目也。」

translations.literal: At the time many generals lost parts of their forces; only Chonggui and Ning returned with their armies intact to camp. Ning proposed submitting the soldiers' merits; Chonggui sighed and said: 'The great general has fallen, and we tally merit—what face have we?'
translations.idiomatic: Most generals had lost men, but Chonggui and Ning brought their forces back intact. When Ning proposed reporting their soldiers' merits, Chonggui sighed and said, "Our commander has fallen—how can we claim credit?"

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 重貴仕至知鄭州，領播州防禦使，改左羽林軍大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: Chonggui served to prefect of Zhengzhou, concurrently defense commissioner of Bozhou, and was changed to Grand General of the Left Forest Army and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui rose to prefect of Zhengzhou and defense commissioner of Bozhou, then retired as Grand General of the Left Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 凝加殿前都虞候，卒，贈彰德軍節度使。

translations.literal: Ning was promoted to Chief Commandant of the Palace Front; on his death he was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was made Chief Commandant of the Palace Front; at his death he was posthumously named military commissioner of the Zhangde army.

sentences.zh: 馬遂，開封人。

translations.literal: Ma Sui was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初隸龍衛軍，補散直，改三班奉職，為北京指使。

translations.literal: At first he was attached to the Dragon Guard Army, appointed irregular attendant, changed to Third-Rank Attendant-in-Service, and became Beijing commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in the Dragon Guard, then as irregular attendant and Third-Rank Attendant-in-Service, and became Beijing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聞王則叛，中夜叱吒，晨起詣留守賈昌朝請擊賊。

translations.literal: On hearing that Wang Ze had rebelled, he shouted in the middle of the night; at dawn he went to the regent Jia Changchao to request attacking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Wang Ze had rebelled, he roused himself in the night; at dawn he went to the regent Jia Changchao and asked to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 昌朝因使持榜入貝州招降，則盛服見之，遂諭以禍福，輒不答。

translations.literal: Changchao therefore had him carry a placard into Beizhou to summon surrender; Ze received him in full dress; Sui then admonished him on fortune and disaster, but he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao sent him into Beizhou with a surrender proclamation. Wang Ze received him in full regalia; Sui urged him on the consequences of rebellion, but Ze would not reply.

sentences.zh: 遂將殺則，而無兵仗自隨。

translations.literal: Sui was about to kill Ze, yet he had brought no arms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui meant to kill Ze, but had brought no weapon.

sentences.zh: 時張得一在側，欲其助己，目得一，得一不動。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Deyi was at his side; he wanted him to help himself and looked at Deyi, but Deyi did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Deyi stood beside him; Sui looked to him for help, but Deyi did not stir.

sentences.zh: 遂奮起，投杯抵則，扼其喉，驅之流血，而左右卒無助之者。

translations.literal: Sui then sprang up, hurled a cup at Ze, seized his throat, and drove him until he bled, yet those beside him in the end had no helper.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sprang up, hurled a cup at Ze, seized his throat, and drew blood—but no one at hand came to his aid.

sentences.zh: 賊黨攢刃聚噪至，斷一臂，猶詈則曰：「妖賊，恨不斬汝萬段！」

translations.literal: Rebel partisans gathered blades and clamored up; they severed one arm, yet he still cursed Ze, saying: 'Demon rebel—I regret not hacking you into ten thousand pieces!'
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rushed in with blades, cut off his arm, yet he still cursed Ze: "Demon rebel—I wish I could hack you to pieces!"

sentences.zh: 賊縛遂廳事前，支解之。

translations.literal: The rebels bound Sui before the hall and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: They bound him before the hall and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 則倉猝被驅駭，傷病數日乃起。

translations.literal: Ze, startled and driven in haste, was injured and ill for several days before he could rise.
translations.idiomatic: Ze, shaken and wounded in the struggle, was ill for days before he could rise.

sentences.zh: 事聞，仁宗歎息久之，贈宮苑使，封其妻為旌忠縣君，賜冠帔，官其子五人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Renzong sighed long; he posthumously made him Palace Park Commissioner, enfeoffed his wife as Lady of Jingzhong County, granted cap and robe, and gave office to his five sons.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Renzong sighed long. He posthumously made Sui Palace Park Commissioner, enfeoffed his wife as Lady of Jingzhong County, granted her court dress, and gave office to his five sons.

sentences.zh: 後得殺遂者驍捷卒石慶，使其子剖心而祭之。

translations.literal: Later they captured Shi Qing, a swift soldier of the Brave and Nimble Corps who had killed Sui, and had his son cut out his heart to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later they captured Shi Qing of the Brave and Nimble Corps, who had killed Sui, and had Sui's son cut out his heart as an offering.

sentences.zh: 董元亨

translations.literal: Dong Yuanheng
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuanheng

sentences.zh: 董元亨，深州束鹿人。

translations.literal: Dong Yuanheng was a man of Shulu in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuanheng was from Shulu in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 累官至國子博士，通判貝州。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he reached Erudite of the Imperial University and was vice-prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Erudite of the Imperial University and served as vice-prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 王則據城叛，是日冬至，元亨方與州將張得一朝謁天慶觀，夜漏未盡，變起倉猝，眾莫知所為。

translations.literal: Wang Ze seized the city and rebelled; that day was the winter solstice; Yuanheng had just been paying morning respects at Tianqing Abbey with the prefectural general Zhang Deyi; the night watch had not ended when the uprising arose suddenly and none knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze seized the city in rebellion. It was the winter solstice; Yuanheng had been at morning rites at Tianqing Abbey with Zhang Deyi when, before dawn, the revolt broke out and no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 元亨促馬馳還，坐廳事，賊党十餘人擐甲露刃，排闥而入，左右皆奔潰。

translations.literal: Yuanheng spurred his horse and galloped back, seated himself in the hall; more than ten rebel partisans donned armor and bared blades, pushed open the doors and entered, and those beside him all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng rode back at once and took his seat in the hall. A dozen rebels in armor burst in with drawn blades; his attendants fled.

sentences.zh: 賊脅元亨曰：「大王遣我來索軍資庫鑰。」

translations.literal: The rebels threatened Yuanheng, saying: 'The Great King sent me to demand the keys to the military stores treasury.'
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threatened him: "The Great King sent us for the keys to the military stores."

sentences.zh: 元亨據案叱之曰：「大王誰也，妖賊乃敢弄兵乎！

translations.literal: Yuanheng leaned on the desk and shouted at them: 'Who is this Great King—a demon rebel who dares to wield arms!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng struck the desk and shouted, "Who is this Great King? A demon rebel dares raise arms!

sentences.zh: 我有死耳，鑰不可得也。」

translations.literal: I have only death; the keys cannot be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: I have only death to offer—you shall not have the keys."

sentences.zh: 賊將郝用繼來，索愈急，曰：「庫帑，今日大王所有也，可不上鑰乎！」

translations.literal: The rebel general Hao Yong came next, demanding more urgently, saying: 'The treasury stores—today they belong to the Great King; will you not hand over the keys!'
translations.idiomatic: The rebel officer Hao Yong came next and pressed harder: "The treasury is the Great King's now—will you not surrender the keys?"

sentences.zh: 元亨厲聲張目罵賊，用遂殺之，賊爭入，攜鑰而去。

translations.literal: Yuanheng in a fierce voice with glaring eyes cursed the rebels; Yong then killed him; the rebels rushed in and carried off the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng cursed them with blazing eyes; Yong killed him, and the rebels rushed in and seized the keys.

sentences.zh: 事聞，仁宗曰：「守法之臣也。」

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Renzong said: 'A minister who upholds the law.'
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Renzong said, "A minister who upheld the law."

sentences.zh: 贈太常少卿，錄其子孫三人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and three of his sons and grandsons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and three of his descendants were given office.

sentences.zh: 賊平，獲郝用，斬以祭元亨。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Hao Yong was captured and beheaded to sacrifice to Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed, Hao Yong was captured and executed as an offering to Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 曹覲，字仲賓，曹修禮子也。

translations.literal: Cao Jin, style name Zhongbin, was the son of Cao Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jin, styled Zhongbin, was the son of Cao Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 叔修古卒，無子，天章閣待制杜杞為言於朝，授覲建州司戶參軍，為修古後。

translations.literal: His uncle Xiugu died without sons; Du Qi, Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion, spoke for him at court; Jin was given office as registrar of Jianzhou and made Xiugu's heir.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Xiugu died childless, Du Qi of the Hanlin spoke for Jin at court; Jin was appointed registrar of Jianzhou and made Xiugu's heir.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，以太子中舍知封州。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era he served as prefect of Fengzhou with the rank of Middle Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era he governed Fengzhou as Middle Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 儂智高叛，攻陷邕管，趨廣州。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao rebelled, attacked and took Yong and Guan, and pressed toward Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao rebelled, he seized Yong and Guan and marched on Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至封州，州人未嘗知兵，士卒才百人，不任戰鬥，又無城隍以守，或勸覲遁去，覲正色叱之曰：「吾守臣也，有死而已，敢言避賊者斬。」

translations.literal: When he reached Fengzhou, the people had never known war; soldiers numbered only a hundred and were unfit for battle; there were no walls and moats to defend; some urged Jin to flee. Jin with stern countenance rebuked them, saying: 'I am a guarding minister; I have only death; whoever dares speak of avoiding the rebels—beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels reached Fengzhou, the people had never seen war; there were barely a hundred soldiers, no walls to defend, and some urged Jin to flee. He rebuked them sternly: "I am the guardian of this prefecture—I have only death to offer. Whoever speaks of flight shall die."

sentences.zh: 麾都監陳曄引兵迎擊賊，封川令率鄉丁、弓手繼進。

translations.literal: He ordered Commandant Chen Ye to lead troops to meet and strike the rebels; the magistrate of Fengchuan led local militia and bowmen to follow in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Commandant Chen Ye to meet the enemy, and the magistrate of Fengchuan led local militia and archers in support.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數百倍，曄兵敗走，鄉丁亦潰。

translations.literal: The rebel host was several hundred times greater; Ye's troops were defeated and fled, and the local militia also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outnumbered them many times over; Chen Ye's force was routed and the militia scattered.

sentences.zh: 覲率從卒決戰不勝，被執。

translations.literal: Jin led his followers in decisive battle but did not prevail and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Jin led his remaining men in a last stand but was captured.

sentences.zh: 賊戒勿殺，捽使拜，且誘之曰：「從我，得美官，付汝兵柄，以女妻汝。」

translations.literal: The rebels warned against killing him, dragged him to make him bow, and moreover tempted him, saying: 'Follow me and you will obtain a fine office; I will give you military authority and marry a daughter to you.'
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forbade his execution, forced him to bow, and tempted him: "Join us and you shall have high office, command of troops, and a wife from among our people."

sentences.zh: 覲不肯拜，且詈曰：「人臣惟北面拜天子，我豈從爾苟生邪！

translations.literal: Jin would not bow and moreover cursed, saying: 'A minister bows only facing north to the Son of Heaven—how should I follow you to live in shame!
translations.idiomatic: Jin refused to bow and cursed them: "A minister bows only to the Son of Heaven facing north—would I live in shame with you?

sentences.zh: 速殺我，幸矣。」

translations.literal: Kill me quickly—that would be fortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: Kill me at once—that would be mercy."

sentences.zh: 賊猶惜不殺，徙置舟中，覲不食者兩日，探懷中印章授其從卒曰：「我且死，若求間道以此上官。」

translations.literal: The rebels still cherished him and did not kill him, moved him onto a boat; Jin did not eat for two days, reached into his breast and took out his seal to give his attendant, saying: 'I am about to die; if you find a secret path, use this to report upward.'
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still spared him and put him aboard a boat. He fasted for two days, then took the seal from his robe and gave it to his attendant: "I am dying. If you find a way out, take this to the authorities."

sentences.zh: 賊知其無降意，害之。

translations.literal: The rebels knew he had no intent to surrender and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he would not yield, they killed him.

sentences.zh: 至死詬賊聲不絕，投屍江中，時年三十五。

translations.literal: Until death his cursing of the rebels did not cease; they cast his body into the river; he was then thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed the rebels without cease until death; they threw his body into the river. He was thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太常少卿，錄其子四人，妻劉避賊死于林峒，追封彭城郡君，加賜冠帔。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; four of his sons were given office; his wife Liu, fleeing the rebels, died in the mountain ravines and was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Pengcheng Commandery with additional grant of cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; four sons were given office. His wife Liu died fleeing the rebels in the hills and was posthumously made Lady of Pengcheng Commandery with court dress.

sentences.zh: 又贈修古尚書工部侍郎，封修古妻陳潁川郡君。

translations.literal: Xiugu was also posthumously made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat, and Xiugu's wife Chen was enfeoffed Lady of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu was posthumously made Vice Minister of Works, and his wife Chen was enfeoffed Lady of Yingchuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 當智高之反，乘嶺南無備，州縣吏往往望風竄匿，故賊所向輒下，獨覲與孔宗旦、趙師旦能以死守。

translations.literal: When Zhigao rebelled, taking advantage of Lingnan's lack of preparation, prefectural and county officials often fled at sight of the wind and hid; therefore wherever the rebels went they took cities, but only Jin, Kong Zongdan, and Zhao Shidan were able to defend unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao rebelled, Lingnan was unprepared and officials often fled at the first rumor; the rebels took city after city—only Jin, Kong Zongdan, and Zhao Shidan held their posts unto death.

sentences.zh: 後田瑜安撫廣南，乃為覲立廟封州。

translations.literal: Later Tian Yu pacified Guangnan and then erected a temple to Jin in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tian Yu pacified Guangnan, a temple to Jin was raised in Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 孔宗旦

translations.literal: Kong Zongdan
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zongdan

sentences.zh: 孔宗旦，魯人，為邕州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Kong Zongdan was a man of Lu and served as registrar of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zongdan was from Lu and served as registrar of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 儂智高未反時，州有白氣出庭中，江水溢，宗旦以為兵象，度智高必反，以書告知州陳珙，珙不聽。

translations.literal: Before Nong Zhigao rebelled, white vapor appeared in the courtyard of the prefecture and the river water overflowed; Zongdan took this as an omen of war, judged that Zhigao would surely rebel, and by letter informed Prefect Chen Gong, but Gong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhigao rebelled, white vapor rose in the prefectural courtyard and the river flooded. Zongdan read these as signs of war and warned Prefect Chen Gong in writing that Zhigao would rebel, but Gong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後智高破橫州，即載其親往桂州，曰：「吾有官守，不得去，無為俱死也。」

translations.literal: Later when Zhigao took Hengzhou, he immediately loaded his kin and sent them to Guizhou, saying: 'I have official duty and cannot leave; do not die together with me.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao took Hengzhou, Zongdan sent his family to Guizhou, saying, "I hold office here and cannot leave—do not die with me."

sentences.zh: 既而州破被執，賊欲任以事，宗旦叱賊，且大罵，遂被害。

translations.literal: Soon after the prefecture fell he was seized; the rebels wished to entrust him with affairs; Zongdan shouted at the rebels and moreover cursed loudly, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured. The rebels wished to employ him, but he rebuked and cursed them until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 始，宗旦官京東，與李師道、徐程、尚同等四人為監司耳目，號為「四瞠」，人多惡之，其後立節如此。

translations.literal: At first, when Zongdan served in Jingdong, he with Li Shidao, Xu Cheng, Shang Tong, and four others were the eyes and ears of the supervisory commissioners, called the 'Four Staring Eyes'; many hated them, yet afterward he established integrity thus.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving in Jingdong, he and Li Shidao, Xu Cheng, Shang Tong, and others had been informants for the supervisory commissioners—called the "Four Staring Eyes"—and were widely hated; yet in the end he showed such integrity.

sentences.zh: 知袁州祖無擇以其事聞，贈太子中允。

translations.literal: Zu Wuse, prefect of Yuanzhou, reported his affair, and he was posthumously made Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Wuse, prefect of Yuanzhou, reported his deeds, and Zongdan was posthumously made Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 趙師旦

translations.literal: Zhao Shidan
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shidan

sentences.zh: 趙師旦字潛叔，樞密副使稹之從子。

translations.literal: Zhao Shidan, style name Qianshu, was the nephew of Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shidan, styled Qianshu, was the nephew of Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhen.

sentences.zh: 美容儀，身長六尺。

translations.literal: He had handsome bearing and was six feet tall.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in bearing and six feet tall.

sentences.zh: 少年頗涉書史，尤刻意刑名之學。

translations.literal: In youth he read widely in books and histories and especially devoted himself to the study of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he read widely in history and devoted himself especially to penal law.

sentences.zh: 用稹蔭，試將作監主簿，累遷甯海軍節度推官。

translations.literal: By Zhen's yin privilege he was tried as master of records in the Directorate of Works and through successive promotions became investigating officer of the Ninghai Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhen's privilege he entered service as master of records in the Directorate of Works and rose to investigating officer of the Ninghai army.

sentences.zh: 知江山縣，斷治出己，吏不能得民一錢，棄物道上，人無敢取。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Jiangshan County he judged from his own judgment; clerks could not take a single cash from the people; goods abandoned on the road—no one dared take them.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jiangshan he judged by his own lights; his clerks could not extort a single coin from the people, and goods left on the road went untouched.

sentences.zh: 以薦者改大理寺丞、知彭城縣，遷太子右贊善大夫，移知康州。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was changed to aide in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Pengcheng County, promoted to Right Supporter-in-Attendance of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to govern Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for merit, he became aide in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Pengcheng, then Right Supporter-in-Attendance of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to govern Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 儂智高破邕州，順流東下，師旦使人覘賊，還報曰：「諸州守皆棄城走矣！」

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao took Yongzhou and flowed east downstream; Shidan sent men to spy on the rebels; they returned and reported: 'The prefects of all prefectures have abandoned their cities and fled!'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao took Yongzhou and marched downstream, Shidan sent scouts who returned reporting, "Every prefect along the river has abandoned his city and fled!"

sentences.zh: 師旦叱曰：「汝亦欲吾走矣。」

translations.literal: Shidan rebuked them, saying: 'You too wish me to flee!'
translations.idiomatic: Shidan rebuked them: "Do you want me to flee as well?"

sentences.zh: 乃大索，得諜者三人，斬以徇。

translations.literal: He then made a great search, obtained three spies, and beheaded them to display as warning.
translations.idiomatic: He searched thoroughly, found three spies, and executed them as a warning.

sentences.zh: 而賊已薄城下，師旦止有兵三百，開門迎戰，殺數十人。

translations.literal: But the rebels had already pressed to the foot of the city; Shidan had only three hundred troops; he opened the gates to meet battle and killed several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were already at the walls. Shidan had only three hundred men; he opened the gates, met them in battle, and killed dozens.

sentences.zh: 會暮，賊稍卻，師旦語其妻，取州印佩之，使負其子以匿，曰：「明日賊必大至，吾知不敵，然不可以去，爾留，死無益也。」

translations.literal: At dusk the rebels withdrew slightly; Shidan spoke to his wife, took the prefectural seal and wore it, had her carry their son to hide, saying: 'Tomorrow the rebels will surely come in force; I know I cannot prevail, yet I cannot leave; if you stay, death is without benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rebels drew back. Shidan told his wife to take the prefectural seal, hide with their son, and said, "Tomorrow they will come in force. I know we cannot win, yet I cannot flee. If you stay, you will die for nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂與監押馬貴部士卒固守州城。

translations.literal: He then with Supervisory Commissioner Ma Gui led the troops in steadfast defense of the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Supervisory Commissioner Ma Gui in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 召貴食，貴不能食，師旦獨飽如平時；

translations.literal: He summoned Gui to eat; Gui could not eat; Shidan alone ate his fill as at ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Shidan summoned Ma Gui to eat. Gui could not eat, but Shidan alone ate his fill as usual.

sentences.zh: 至夜，貴臥不安席，師旦即臥內大鼾。

translations.literal: When night came, Gui could not rest on his bed; Shidan immediately lay down within the bedchamber and snored loudly.
translations.idiomatic: That night Ma Gui tossed sleeplessly on his bed, while Shidan lay down at once and slept heavily, snoring.

sentences.zh: 遲明，賊攻城愈急，左右請少避，師旦曰：「戰死與戮死何如？」

translations.literal: At dawn the rebels pressed the siege ever harder; those beside him asked to withdraw slightly; Shidan said: "How does dying in battle compare with dying by execution?"
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the rebels pressed the attack harder. His attendants urged him to withdraw somewhat. Shidan said, "What is the difference between dying in battle and dying by execution?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「願為國家死。」

translations.literal: All said together: "We wish to die for the state."
translations.idiomatic: All replied, "We are willing to die for the realm."

sentences.zh: 至城破無一人逃者。

translations.literal: When the city fell, not one person fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, not a single man fled.

sentences.zh: 矢盡，與貴俱還，據堂而坐。

translations.literal: When arrows were exhausted, he together with Gui both returned and, occupying the hall, sat.
translations.idiomatic: When their arrows were spent, he and Ma Gui withdrew to the hall and sat down.

sentences.zh: 智高麾兵鼓噪爭入，脅師旦，師旦大罵曰：「餓獠，朝廷負若何事，乃敢反邪！

translations.literal: Zhigao waved his troops who clamored and rushed in, threatened Shidan, and Shidan cursed loudly, saying: "Starving savages! What has the court ever wronged you in, that you dare rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao waved his troops forward in a roaring rush. They seized Shidan, and he cursed them: "You starving savages! What wrong has the court ever done you, that you dare rebel?

sentences.zh: 天子發一校兵，汝無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven sends a single detachment of troops, you will not leave a survivor among you."
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor sends one regiment, not one of you will survive."

sentences.zh: 智高怒，並貴害之。

translations.literal: Zhigao was enraged and together with Gui killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zhigao had both of them killed.

sentences.zh: 賊既去，州人為立廟。

translations.literal: After the rebels departed, the people of the prefecture erected a temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels left, the people of the prefecture built a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 事平，贈光祿少卿，賜其母王長安縣太君冠帔，錄其子弟並從子三人。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Household; his mother Lady Wang was granted the rank of Lady of Chang'an County with cap and sash; his sons and younger brothers together with three nephews were given office.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Household; his mother, Lady Wang, was granted the rank of Lady of Chang'an County with ceremonial cap and sash; and his sons, younger brothers, and three nephews were given official appointments.

sentences.zh: 師旦遇害時，年四十二。

translations.literal: When Shidan met calamity, he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shidan was forty-two when he was killed.

sentences.zh: 柩過江山，江山之人迎師旦喪，哭祭于路，絡繹數百里不絕。

translations.literal: When the coffin passed through Jiangshan, the people of Jiangshan welcomed Shidan's funeral procession, weeping and offering sacrifice on the road, continuous for several hundred li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin passed through Jiangshan, the people of that county came out to receive his funeral train, weeping and offering sacrifice along the road for hundreds of li without end.

sentences.zh: 同時有王從政者，以東頭供奉官、閣門祗候，與儂智高戰于太平場，被執，罵賊不已，至以沸湯沃之，終不屈而死。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Wang Congzheng, who as an Eastern Head Presentation Officer and Palace Gate Usher fought Nong Zhigao at Taiping Field, was seized, cursed the rebels without ceasing, until boiling water was poured on him, yet in the end he did not yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time one Wang Congzheng, an Eastern Head Presentation Officer and Palace Gate Usher, fought Zhigao at Taiping Field. Captured, he kept cursing the rebels; they poured boiling water over him, yet he never yielded and died.

sentences.zh: 贈信州刺史，錄其孫二人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made prefect of Xinzhou, and two of his grandsons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made prefect of Xinzhou, and two grandsons were given official appointments.

sentences.zh: 蘇緘，字宣甫，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Su Jian, style name Xuanfu, was a man of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jian, styled Xuanfu, was from Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調廣州南海主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as chief clerk of Nanhai in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Nanhai in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州領蕃舶，每商至，則擇官閱實其貲，商皆豪家大姓，習以客禮見主者，緘以選往，商樊氏輒升階就席，緘詰而杖之。

translations.literal: The prefecture supervised foreign merchant ships; whenever merchants arrived, an official was chosen to inspect and verify their goods; the merchants were all powerful great clans, accustomed to receiving the chief with guest courtesy; Jian went by selection; the merchant Fan clan forthwith ascended the steps and took a seat; Jian questioned and beat him with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou oversaw foreign shipping, and when merchants arrived an official was assigned to inspect their cargo. These merchants were wealthy powerful families accustomed to being received as guests. When Jian was sent to perform this duty, a merchant surnamed Fan walked straight up and took a seat. Jian questioned him and beat him with a staff.

sentences.zh: 樊訴於州，州召責緘，緘曰：「主簿雖卑，邑官也，商雖富，部民也，邑官杖部民，有何不可？」

translations.literal: Fan complained to the prefecture; the prefecture summoned and reprimanded Jian; Jian said: "Though the chief clerk is lowly, he is a district official; though the merchant is rich, he is a subject of the district; for a district official to beat a district subject—what is impermissible about it?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan complained to the prefecture, which summoned and rebuked Jian. Jian said, "The chief clerk's rank is low, but he is an officer of the district. The merchant is rich, but he is a subject of the district. What is wrong with a district officer beating a district subject?"

sentences.zh: 州不能詰。

translations.literal: The prefecture could not interrogate further.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had no answer.

sentences.zh: 再調陽武尉，劇盜李囊橐於民，賊曹莫能捕。

translations.literal: Reassigned to Yangwu as commandant, the bold bandit Li plundered among the people, and the bandit-catchers could not seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned as commandant of Yangwu, he faced a notorious bandit named Li who robbed the people, and the police could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 緘訪得其處，萃眾大索，火旁舍以迫之。

translations.literal: Jian inquired and found his whereabouts, gathered the crowd in a great search, and set fire to a neighboring building to force him out.
translations.idiomatic: Jian tracked him down, gathered men for a thorough search, and set fire to a neighboring house to flush him out.

sentences.zh: 李從中逸出，緘馳馬逐，斬其首送府。

translations.literal: Li escaped from the midst; Jian galloped after him, beheaded him, and sent the head to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Li broke out from the middle of the search. Jian chased him on horseback, cut off his head, and sent it to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 府尹賈昌朝驚曰：「儒者乃爾輕生邪！」

translations.literal: Prefect Jia Changchao in alarm said: "Can a scholar be so reckless with his life!"
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Jia Changchao exclaimed in astonishment, "Would a scholar really risk his life like this?"

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞，知英州。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became secretary in the Archive and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to secretary in the Archive and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 儂智高圍廣，緘曰：「廣，吾都府也，且去州近，今城危在旦暮而不往救，非義也。」

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao besieged Guang; Jian said: "Guang is my superior prefecture, and moreover is near my own prefecture; now the city faces peril from one dawn to the next yet I do not go to rescue—this is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao besieged Guang, Jian said, "Guang is my superior prefecture and lies close to my post. The city may fall at any moment, and not to go to its aid would be unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 即募士數千人，委印于提點刑獄鮑軻，夜行赴難，去廣二十里止營。

translations.literal: He immediately recruited several thousand warriors, entrusted his seal to Circuit Intendant for Penal Affairs Bao Ke, marched by night to the crisis, and halted camp twenty li from Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately raised several thousand men, entrusted his seal to Circuit Intendant for Penal Affairs Bao Ke, marched through the night to the rescue, and camped twenty li from Guang.

sentences.zh: 廣人黃師宓陷賊中，為之謀主，緘擒斬其父。

translations.literal: A man of Guang, Huang Shimi, was trapped among the rebels and served as their chief strategist; Jian seized and beheaded his father.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shimi of Guang had joined the rebels as their chief strategist. Jian captured and executed his father.

sentences.zh: 群不逞並緣為盜，復捕殺六十餘人，招其詿誤者六千八百人，使復業。

translations.literal: A crowd of lawless men together took the opportunity to become bandits; he again captured and killed more than sixty, and summoned more than six thousand eight hundred who had been misled, causing them to resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Mobs of ruffians took advantage of the turmoil to turn bandit. He captured and killed more than sixty and summoned back more than six thousand eight hundred who had been misled, restoring them to their trades.

sentences.zh: 賊勢沮，將解去，緘分兵先扼其歸路，布槎木亙四十里。

translations.literal: The rebel strength was checked and they were about to withdraw; Jian divided troops to first block their route of return, deploying rafts and logs stretching forty li.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel momentum faltered and they prepared to withdraw, Jian sent detachments to cut off their retreat, blocking the route with rafts and logs for forty li.

sentences.zh: 賊至不得前，乃繞出數舍渡江，由連、賀而西。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived they could not advance, so they went around several dwellings, crossed the river, and went west by way of Lian and He.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked from advancing, the rebels detoured several miles, crossed the river, and fled west through Lian and He.

sentences.zh: 緘與賊戰，摧傷甚眾，盡得其所掠物。

translations.literal: Jian fought the rebels, crushing and wounding a great many, and fully recovered what they had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fought them, inflicting heavy casualties and recovering all their loot.

sentences.zh: 時諸將皆罷，獨緘有功，仁宗喜，換為供備庫副使、廣東都監，管押兩路兵甲，遣中使賜朝衣、金帶。

translations.literal: At the time all the generals were dismissed; Jian alone had merit; Emperor Renzong was pleased; he was transferred to be Deputy Commissioner of the Supplies-Preparedness Vault and Guangdong Chief Inspector, managing and escorting military equipment of the two circuits; an imperial envoy was sent to bestow court robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When the other generals were dismissed, Jian alone had distinguished himself. Emperor Renzong was pleased and transferred him to Deputy Commissioner of the Supplies-Preparedness Vault and Guangdong Chief Inspector, placing him in charge of military equipment for both circuits; an imperial envoy was sent with court robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 襲賊至邕，大將陳曙以失律誅，緘亦貶房州司馬。

translations.literal: When the rebels raided as far as Yong, the great general Chen Shu was executed for violating military discipline, and Jian was also demoted to military aide of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels struck Yong, the commanding general Chen Shu was executed for disciplinary failure, and Jian was demoted to military aide of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復著作佐郎，監越州稅十餘年，始還副使。

translations.literal: Restored as editorial assistant, he supervised the tax of Yuezhou for more than ten years before he was finally restored to deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Restored as editorial assistant, he oversaw Yuezhou's taxes for more than ten years before recovering his deputy commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 知廉州，屋多茅竹，戍卒楊禧醉焚營，延燒民廬，因乘以為竊，緘戮之於市，又坐謫潭州都監。

translations.literal: As prefect of Lianzhou, where houses were mostly thatch and bamboo, garrison soldier Yang Xi drunkenly burned the camp, the fire spreading to burn civilian dwellings; taking advantage of this he turned to theft; Jian executed him in the market, and was again demoted to Chief Inspector of Tanzhou for this.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Lianzhou, where buildings were mostly bamboo and thatch, garrison soldier Yang Xi, drunk, set fire to the camp; the blaze spread to civilians' homes, and he looted amid the chaos. Jian had him executed in the market, but was himself demoted to Chief Inspector of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知鼎州。

translations.literal: Before long, he governed Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，進如京使、廣東鈴轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, he was promoted to Capital Envoy and Guangdong Controller.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era he was promoted to Capital Envoy and Guangdong Controller.

sentences.zh: 四年，交阯謀入寇，以緘為皇城使知邕州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Jiaozhi plotted an invasion; Jian was made Imperial City Envoy and prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Jiaozhi plotted an invasion, and Jian was made Imperial City Envoy and prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 緘伺得實，以書抵知桂州沈起，起不以為意。

translations.literal: Jian secretly verified the truth and by letter notified Shen Qi, prefect of Guizhou; Qi did not take it seriously.
translations.idiomatic: Jian confirmed the intelligence and wrote to Shen Qi, prefect of Guizhou, but Qi paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 及劉彝代起，緘致書於彝，請罷所行事。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi replaced Qi, Jian sent a letter to Yi requesting that the matters being carried out be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi replaced Qi, Jian wrote to Yi asking him to halt the project.

sentences.zh: 彝不聽，反移文責緘沮議，令勿得輒言。

translations.literal: Yi would not listen and instead sent an official communication rebuking Jian for obstructing deliberation, ordering that he must not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused and instead issued an official rebuke, accusing Jian of obstructing policy and forbidding him to speak out again.

sentences.zh: 八年，蠻遂入寇，眾號八萬，陷欽、廉，破邕四砦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the barbarians then invaded; their force was claimed at eighty thousand; they took Qin and Lian and broke four Yong forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the barbarians invaded in force, claiming eighty thousand men. They took Qin and Lian and overran four Yong forts.

sentences.zh: 緘聞其至，閱州兵得二千八百，召僚吏與郡人之材者，授以方略，勒部隊，使分地自守。

translations.literal: When Jian heard they had arrived, he reviewed the prefectural troops and obtained twenty-eight hundred; he summoned staff officials and capable men of the prefecture, gave them strategy, arrayed the units, and had them each defend their own sector.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of their approach, Jian mustered twenty-eight hundred prefectural troops, summoned capable officials and local men, instructed them in strategy, and deployed the units to defend separate sectors.

sentences.zh: 民驚震四出，緘悉出官帑及私藏示之曰：「吾兵械既具，蓄聚不乏，今賊已薄城，宜固守以遲外援。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed and scattered in all directions; Jian fully produced the official treasury and his private stores to show them, saying: "Our arms are already prepared and stores are not lacking; now the rebels have pressed close to the city—we should hold fast to delay for outside relief.
translations.idiomatic: The people panicked and fled in all directions. Jian displayed the official treasury and his private stores and said, "Our arms are ready and our supplies ample. The enemy is at the walls; we must hold firm and wait for relief.

sentences.zh: 若一人舉足，則群心搖矣，幸聽吾言，敢越佚則孥戮汝。」

translations.literal: If one person moves a foot, then the minds of the crowd will waver; I hope you heed my words—whoever dares to flee, I will execute you and your families."
translations.idiomatic: If even one person runs, every heart will fail. Obey me: anyone who tries to flee will be executed, along with his family."

sentences.zh: 有大校翟績潛出，斬以徇，由是上下脅息。

translations.literal: A major commander Zhai Ji secretly went out; he was beheaded to display as warning; from this above and below were awed into silence.
translations.idiomatic: A major commander named Zhai Ji tried to slip away; Jian beheaded him as a warning, and from then on none dared stir.

sentences.zh: 緘子子元為桂州司戶，因公事攜妻子來省，欲還而寇至。

translations.literal: Jian's son Ziyuan was registrar of Guizhou; on official business he brought wife and children to visit; he wished to return but the invaders arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Ziyuan, registrar of Guizhou, had come on official business with his wife and children to visit; he wished to return, but the invaders arrived.

sentences.zh: 緘念人不可戶曉，必以郡守家出城，乃獨遣子元，留其妻子。

translations.literal: Jian thought people could not be instructed household by household; if the prefect's family left the city it would surely cause panic; therefore he sent Ziyuan alone and kept his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Jian knew he could not reason with every household and that if the prefect's family fled the city, morale would collapse. He sent Ziyuan out alone and kept his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 選勇士拿舟逆戰，斬蠻酋二。

translations.literal: He selected brave warriors to take boats and meet the enemy in battle, beheading two barbarian chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He picked brave men to take boats and fight upstream, killing two barbarian chiefs.

sentences.zh: 邕既受圍，緘晝夜行勞士卒，發神臂弓射賊，所殪甚眾。

translations.literal: Once Yong was besieged, Jian day and night went about encouraging the troops, deploying divine-arm crossbows to shoot the rebels, killing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yong was besieged, Jian day and night encouraged his troops and used divine-arm crossbows against the rebels, killing many.

sentences.zh: 緘初求救于劉彝，彝遣將張守節救之，逗遛不進。

translations.literal: Jian at first begged Liu Yi for rescue; Yi sent the general Zhang Shoujie to save him, but he lingered and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jian first asked Liu Yi for help. Yi sent General Zhang Shoujie, but Zhang dallied and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 緘又以蠟書告急于提點刑獄宋球，球得書驚泣，督守節。

translations.literal: Jian again by wax-sealed letter urgently informed Circuit Intendant for Penal Affairs Song Qiu; Qiu received the letter, wept in alarm, and urged Shoujie forward.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also sent an urgent message in a wax-sealed letter to Circuit Intendant Song Qiu. Qiu wept when he read it and pressed Shoujie to march.

sentences.zh: 守節皇恐，遽移屯大夾嶺，回保昆侖關，猝遇賊，不及陣，舉軍皆覆。

translations.literal: Shoujie in panic hastily moved camp to Great Jia Ridge, turned back to hold Kunlun Pass, suddenly encountered the rebels, had no time to form ranks, and the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujie panicked, hurried to Great Jia Ridge, and fell back to defend Kunlun Pass. He suddenly met the enemy, had no time to form ranks, and his entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 蠻獲北軍，知其善攻城，啖以利，使為雲梯，又為攻濠洞子，蒙以華布，緘悉焚之。

translations.literal: The barbarians captured Northern Army troops, knew they were skilled at siege, tempted them with profit, had them make scaling ladders, and also made trench-attack engines covered with fine cloth; Jian burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians captured Song troops skilled at siege, bribed them to build scaling ladders and covered trench-assault engines, and Jian burned them all.

sentences.zh: 蠻計已窮，將引去，而知外援不至，或教賊囊土傅城者，頃刻高數丈，蟻附而登，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The barbarians' plans were exhausted and they were about to withdraw, but learning outside relief did not come, someone taught the rebels to bag earth and pile it against the wall; in an instant it rose several zhang; they climbed like ants and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Their plans exhausted, the barbarians were about to withdraw until they learned no relief was coming. Someone showed them how to fill sacks with earth and pile them against the wall; within moments the mound rose several zhang. They swarmed up like ants, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 緘猶領傷卒馳騎戰愈厲，而力不敵，乃曰：「吾義不死賊手。」

translations.literal: Jian still led wounded troops galloping to fight ever more fiercely, but strength could not match; he then said: "In righteousness I shall not die at the rebels' hands."
translations.idiomatic: Jian still led his wounded men in fierce mounted combat but could not prevail. He said, "Righteousness forbids that I die in the enemy's hands."

sentences.zh: 亟還州治，殺其家三十六人，藏於坎，縱火自焚。

translations.literal: He hastily returned to the prefectural seat, killed his family of thirty-six persons, hid them in a pit, and set fire to burn himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried back to the prefectural seat, killed thirty-six members of his household, hid their bodies in a pit, and set himself on fire.

sentences.zh: 蠻至，求屍皆不得，屠郡民五萬餘人，率百人為一積，凡五百八十餘積，隤三州城以填江。

translations.literal: When the barbarians arrived, they sought corpses but could find none; they slaughtered more than fifty thousand prefectural people, generally making piles of a hundred each, in all more than five hundred eighty piles, and demolished three circuit cities to fill the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians arrived they could find no bodies. They slaughtered more than fifty thousand people of the prefecture, stacked the dead in piles of a hundred—more than five hundred eighty piles in all—and demolished three circuit cities to fill the river.

sentences.zh: 邕被圍四十二日，糧盡泉涸，人吸漚麻水以濟渴，多病下痢，相枕藉以死，然訖無一叛者。

translations.literal: Yong was besieged forty-two days; grain was exhausted and springs dried; people drank fermented hemp water to slake thirst; many suffered dysentery and died lying one upon another, yet to the end not one betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was besieged for forty-two days. Food ran out and the springs dried up; people drank fermented hemp water to quench thirst; dysentery killed them in heaps; yet not one man defected.

sentences.zh: 緘憤沈起、劉彝致寇，又不救患，欲上疏論之。

translations.literal: Jian resented that Shen Qi and Liu Yi had brought on the invasion and had not saved the crisis; he wished to submit a memorial discussing this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian blamed Shen Qi and Liu Yi for bringing on the invasion and failing to send relief, and wished to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 屬道梗不通，乃榜其罪于市，冀朝廷得聞焉。

translations.literal: Since the roads were blocked and impassable, he posted their crimes in the market, hoping the court might hear.
translations.idiomatic: With roads blocked he could not reach the capital, so he posted their crimes in the marketplace, hoping word would reach the court.

sentences.zh: 神宗聞緘死，嗟悼，贈奉國軍節度使，諡曰忠勇，賜都城甲第五、鄉里上田十頃，聽其家自擇。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong heard of Jian's death and sighed in grief; he was posthumously made military commissioner of the Fengguo Army; his posthumous title was Loyal and Brave; five mansions in the capital and ten qing of premium farmland in his home district were granted, allowing his family to choose for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong learned of Jian's death he mourned him deeply. Jian was posthumously made military commissioner of the Fengguo Army with the posthumous title Loyal and Brave. The court granted his family five mansions in the capital and ten qing of premium farmland at home, to be chosen as they wished.

sentences.zh: 以子元為西頭供奉官、閣門祗候，召對，謂曰：「邕管賴卿父守禦，儻如欽、廉即破，則賊乘勝奔突，桂、象皆不得保矣。

translations.literal: Ziyuan was made Western Head Presentation Officer and Palace Gate Usher; summoned for audience; the emperor said: "Yong's defense relied on your father's defense; if like Qin and Lian it had fallen at once, then the rebels would have seized victory and burst forth, and Gui and Xiang could none be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan was made Western Head Presentation Officer and Palace Gate Usher and summoned to audience. The emperor said, "Yong survived because your father held it. Had it fallen as quickly as Qin and Lian, the enemy would have surged forward and neither Gui nor Xiang could have been saved.

sentences.zh: 昔張巡、許遠以睢陽蔽遮江、淮，較之卿父，不能過也。」

translations.literal: In former times Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan with Suiyang screened and shielded the Yangzi and Huai; compared with your father, they cannot surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan once held Suiyang and shielded the Yangzi and Huai regions. Your father ranks no lower than they."

sentences.zh: 改授殿中丞，通判邕州。

translations.literal: He was changed and appointed Palace Assistant-in-Censorate and Vice-Prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan was appointed Palace Assistant-in-Censorate and vice-prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 次子子明、子正，孫廣淵、直溫，與緘同死，皆褒贈焉。

translations.literal: The second sons Ziming and Zizheng, grandsons Guangyuan and Zhiven, together with Jian died the same death; all were ennobled posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: The second sons Ziming and Zizheng and grandsons Guangyuan and Zhiven died with Jian and were all posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 起與彝皆坐謫官。

translations.literal: Qi and Yi both were demoted on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qi and Liu Yi were both demoted.

sentences.zh: 緘沒後，交人謀寇桂州，行數舍，其眾見大兵從北來，呼曰：「蘇皇城領兵來報怨。」

translations.literal: After Jian's death, the Jiaozhi people plotted to invade Guizhou; they marched several dwellings; their multitude saw a great army coming from the north and cried: "Imperial City Envoy Su leads troops to take revenge."
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's death the people of Jiaozhi plotted to invade Guizhou. After marching several miles their troops saw a great army approaching from the north and cried, "Imperial City Envoy Su leads an army to avenge himself!"

sentences.zh: 懼而引歸。

translations.literal: Fearful, they withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, they turned back.

sentences.zh: 邕人為緘立祠，元祐中賜額懷忠。

translations.literal: The people of Yong erected a shrine to Jian; in the Yuanyou era the plaque "Cherishing Loyalty" was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yong built a shrine to Jian; in the Yuanyou era it was granted the plaque name Cherishing Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 秦傳序

translations.literal: Qin Chuanxu
translations.idiomatic: Qin Chuanxu

sentences.zh: 秦傳序，江寧人。

translations.literal: Qin Chuanxu was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Chuanxu was from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，充夔峽巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he served as inspector of the Kui and Xia passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he served as inspector of the Kui and Xia passes.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，賊眾奄至，傅夔州城下，傳序督士卒晝夜拒戰，嬰城既久，危蹙日甚，長吏皆奔竄投賊。

translations.literal: At Li Shun's rebellion, rebel forces suddenly arrived and reached beneath the walls of Kuizhou; Chuanxu supervised the troops day and night in resisting battle; besieged in the city for long, peril pressed daily ever tighter; senior officials all fled in panic and joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shun's rebellion rebel forces suddenly appeared before Kuizhou. Chuanxu led his troops in day-and-night defense. As the siege wore on and danger mounted, the senior officials all fled and joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 傳序謂士卒曰：「吾為監軍，盡死節以守城，吾之職也，安可苟免乎！」

translations.literal: Chuanxu said to the troops: "I serve as supervisory commissioner; to exhaust integrity unto death to hold the city is my duty—how can I seek to escape cheaply!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuanxu told his troops, "I am the supervisory commissioner. To die holding this city is my duty. How can I seek to save myself?"

sentences.zh: 城中乏食，傳序出囊橐服玩，盡市酒肉以犒士卒，慰勉之，眾皆感泣力戰。

translations.literal: Food in the city was lacking; Chuanxu brought out his purse, bags, garments, and curios, fully exchanged them for wine and meat to reward the troops, consoled and encouraged them; the crowd all were moved to tears and fought with effort.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran short. Chuanxu sold his personal belongings for wine and meat to reward his men, encouraged them, and all wept as they fought on.

sentences.zh: 傳序度力不能拒，乃為蠟書遣人間道上言：「臣盡死力，誓不降賊。」

translations.literal: Chuanxu judged strength could not resist; he then made a wax-sealed letter and sent a man by secret path to report above: "Your servant exerts death's utmost strength and vows not to surrender to the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing resistance was hopeless, he sent a wax-sealed letter by a secret route: "Your servant will fight to the death and vows never to surrender."

sentences.zh: 城壞，傳序赴火死。

translations.literal: The walls were broken; Chuanxu went to the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the walls collapsed, Chuanxu threw himself into the flames and died.

sentences.zh: 傳序家寄荊湖間，子奭溯峽求父屍，溺死。

translations.literal: Chuanxu's family was lodged in the Jing-Hu region; his son Shi went upstream through the gorges seeking his father's corpse and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanxu's family lived in the Jing-Hu region. His son Shi went upriver through the gorges searching for his father's body and drowned.

sentences.zh: 人以為父死于忠，子死於孝。

translations.literal: People took it that the father died in loyalty and the son died in filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: People said the father had died for loyalty and the son for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 奏至，太宗嗟惻久之，錄傳序次子煦為殿直，以錢十萬賜其家。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Taizong sighed in compassion for long and enrolled Chuanxu's second son Xu as palace guard; one hundred thousand cash was granted to his family.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Emperor Taizong mourned him deeply. Chuanxu's second son Xu was given office as a palace guard, and one hundred thousand cash was granted to the family.

sentences.zh: 煦卒，復以煦弟昉為三班奉職。

translations.literal: When Xu died, Xu's younger brother Fang was again made a Three-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu died, his younger brother Fang was appointed a Three-Rank Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詹良臣

translations.literal: Zhan Liangchen
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Liangchen

sentences.zh: 詹良臣，字元公，睦州分水人。

translations.literal: Zhan Liangchen, style name Yuangong, was a man of Fenshui in Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Liangchen, styled Yuangong, was from Fenshui in Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不第，以恩得官，調縉雲縣尉。

translations.literal: He failed the jinshi examination, gained office by grace, and was assigned as commandant of Jinyun County.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination, received office by privilege, and was appointed commandant of Jinyun County.

sentences.zh: 方臘起，其党洪再犯處州，守貳俱棄城遁。

translations.literal: When Fang La rose, his partisan Hong again attacked Chuzhou; the prefect and vice-prefect both abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rebelled, his follower Hong again attacked Chuzhou; the prefect and vice-prefect both abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 又有他盜霍成富者，用臘年號，剽掠縉雲。

translations.literal: There was also another bandit Huo Chenfu who used La's reign title and plundered Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Another bandit, Huo Chenfu, adopted La's reign title and raided Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 良臣曰：「捕盜，尉職也，縱不勝，敢愛死乎？」

translations.literal: Liangchen said: "Catching bandits is the commandant's duty; even if I cannot prevail, how would I dare spare my life?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen said, "Catching bandits is a commandant's duty. Even if I cannot win, how can I shrink from death?"

sentences.zh: 率弓兵數十人出禦之，為所執。

translations.literal: He led several tens of bow troops out to resist and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He led several dozen archers out to fight and was captured.

sentences.zh: 成富誘使降，良臣曰：「汝輩不知求生，顧欲降我邪！

translations.literal: Chenfu tried to induce surrender; Liangchen said: "You lot do not know to seek life yet wish to make me surrender!
translations.idiomatic: Chenfu tried to win him over. Liangchen said, "You fools do not know enough to save your own lives, yet you think you can make me surrender?

sentences.zh: 昔年李順反于蜀，王倫反于淮南，王則反于貝州，身首橫分，妻子與同惡，無少長皆誅死，旦暮官軍至，汝肉飼狗鼠矣。」

translations.literal: In former years Li Shun rebelled in Shu, Wang Lun in Huainan, Wang Ze in Beizhou—bodies and heads split apart, wives and children together with fellow evildoers, none young or old spared from execution; morning and evening the official army will arrive and your flesh will feed dogs and rats."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun rebelled in Shu, Wang Lun in Huainan, Wang Ze in Beizhou—they were torn limb from limb, and their families and accomplices, young and old, were all executed. The imperial army will come any day, and your flesh will feed the dogs and rats."

sentences.zh: 賊怒，臠其肉，使自啖之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged, sliced his flesh, and made him eat it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels cut flesh from his body and forced him to eat it.

sentences.zh: 良臣吐且罵，至死不絕聲，見者掩面流涕，時年七十二。

translations.literal: Liangchen spat and cursed, to death without ceasing sound; those who saw covered their faces and wept; he was seventy-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen spat and cursed without cease until he died. Onlookers covered their faces and wept. He was seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 徽宗聞而傷之，贈通直郎，官其子孫二人。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong heard and grieved; he was posthumously made Direct Attendant; two of his sons and grandsons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong heard of it he was deeply grieved. Liangchen was posthumously made Direct Attendant, and two of his descendants were given official appointments.

sentences.zh: 江仲明

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongming
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongming

sentences.zh: 江仲明，台州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongming was a man of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongming was from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和寇亂，載老母逃山澗中，猝遇寇於東城之岡，逼使就降，仲明義不辱，奮起罵賊，卒死之，丞相呂賾浩誄以文。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe bandit turmoil, carrying his old mother he fled into mountain ravines; he suddenly met bandits at the hill of East City; they forced him to surrender; Zhongming, righteous and unwilling to be shamed, rose up cursing the bandits and finally died; Chancellor Lü Yihao eulogized him in prose.
translations.idiomatic: During the bandit turmoil of the Xuanhe era he fled with his elderly mother into the mountains. He suddenly met bandits on the hill east of the city. They forced him to surrender, but Zhongming, unwilling to suffer disgrace, rose up cursing them and was killed. Chancellor Lü Yihao composed a eulogy for him.

sentences.zh: 有蔣煜者，州之仙居人，有文學。

translations.literal: There was one Jiang Yu, from Xianju in the prefecture, with literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Jiang Yu, a man of Xianju in the prefecture, learned in letters.

sentences.zh: 寇欲妻以女，煜拒之，脅以拜，亦不從，寇曰：「吾戮汝矣！」

translations.literal: The bandits wished to marry their daughter to him; Yu refused; they threatened to make him bow yet he would not comply; the bandits said: "I will execute you!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits wished to marry him to a daughter; Yu refused. They threatened him to bow, but he still would not comply. The bandits said, "I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 煜伸頸就刃，詈聲不絕而死。

translations.literal: Yu extended his neck to meet the blade, cursing without cease until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu thrust out his neck to the blade and died cursing without pause.

sentences.zh: 李若水

translations.literal: Li Ruoshui
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruoshui

sentences.zh: 李若水，字清卿，洺州曲周人，元名若冰。

translations.literal: Li Ruoshui, style name Qingqing, was a man of Quzhou in Mozhou; his original name was Ruobing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruoshui, styled Qingqing, was from Quzhou in Mozhou; he had originally been named Ruobing.

sentences.zh: 上舍登第，調元城尉、平陽府司錄。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations from the Upper Hall and was assigned as commandant of Yuancheng and recorder of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Upper Hall examination and was appointed commandant of Yuancheng and recorder of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 試學官第一，濟南教授，除太學博士。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the academic official examination, served as instructor at Jinan, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the academic official examination, served as instructor at Jinan, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 蔡京晚復相，子絛用事，李邦彥不平，欲謝病去。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing again became chief councilor in his later years, his son Cai Tiao wielded power; Li Bangyan was discontent and wished to resign on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to the chief councilorship in his later years, his son Cai Tiao held sway; Li Bangyan was aggrieved and wished to resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 若水為言：「大臣以道事君，不可則止，胡不取決上前，使去就之義，暴於天下。

translations.literal: Ruoshui spoke to him: "Great ministers serve the ruler by the Way—when they cannot, they should stop. Why not seek resolution before the throne, so that the principle of staying or leaving be made plain to all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui told him, "Great ministers serve the ruler by the Way, and when they cannot, they should withdraw. Why not settle the matter before the throne, so that the right to stay or go is made plain to the realm?

sentences.zh: 顧可默默托疾而退，使天下有伴食之譏邪？」

translations.literal: How can one silently plead illness and withdraw, inviting the reproach throughout the realm of being a mere attendant at court?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you quietly plead illness and slip away, inviting the whole realm to call you a useless hanger-on at court?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「積蠹已久，致理惟難。

translations.literal: He also said: "Corruption has accumulated for long; achieving good governance is exceedingly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Rot has piled up for years, and good order is hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 建裁損而邦用未豐，省科徭而民力猶困，權貴抑而益橫，仕流濫而莫澄。

translations.literal: Expenditures have been cut yet state revenues are not ample; taxes and corvée reduced yet the people's strength is still strained; when the powerful are restrained they become still more overbearing; the official ranks overflow yet none are cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Cuts have been ordered yet the treasury is still thin; taxes and corvée have been reduced yet the people remain exhausted; restrain the powerful and they grow bolder still; the official ranks are swollen yet never cleared.

sentences.zh: 正宜置驛求賢，解榻待士，采其寸長遠見，以興治功。」

translations.literal: This is precisely the time to post relay stations to seek the worthy, spread one's couch to welcome scholars, gather even their inch of talent and far-sighted views, and thereby raise up achievements in governance."
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to post relays to seek talent, open one's door to scholars, draw on whatever insight they offer, and use it to restore good government."

sentences.zh: 凡十數端，皆深中時病，邦彥不悅。

translations.literal: In all more than ten points, each struck deeply at the ailments of the age; Bangyan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In more than ten such points he struck deep at the ills of the day, and Bangyan was displeased.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，為太學博士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, he served as Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingkang reign, he served as Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司高俅死，故事，天子當掛服舉哀，若水言：「俅以幸臣躐躋顯位，敗壞軍政，金人長驅，其罪當與童貫等。

translations.literal: When Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies Gao Qiu died, by precedent the Son of Heaven should don mourning garments and perform lamentation rites. Ruoshui said: "Qiu, by virtue of a favorite minister, leaped to eminent rank, ruined military governance, and let the Jurchens drive straight in—his crime should be ranked with Tong Guan and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Qiu, Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, died, precedent called for the emperor to don mourning and perform lamentation rites. Ruoshui said, "Qiu rose to high rank as a favorite, ruined military affairs, and let the Jurchens sweep in unchecked. His guilt ranks with Tong Guan and men like him.

sentences.zh: 得全首領以沒，尚當追削官秩，示與眾棄；

translations.literal: Even to die with his head intact, his offices should still be posthumously stripped, showing that all have cast him off;
translations.idiomatic: Even though he died whole, his ranks should still be posthumously stripped, to show that all have cast him off;

sentences.zh: 而有司循常習故，欲加縟禮，非所以靖公議也。」

translations.literal: yet the responsible officials follow routine and custom, wishing to add elaborate rites—this is not the way to still public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: yet the officials follow old custom and would add elaborate rites. That is no way to quiet public outrage."

sentences.zh: 章再上，乃止。

translations.literal: He submitted his memorial twice before they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his memorial twice before the court desisted.

sentences.zh: 欽宗將遣使至金國，議以賦入贖三鎮，詔舉可使者，若水在選中。
