translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong was about to send envoys to the Jin state; they deliberated redeeming the Three Prefectures with tax revenues; an edict called for nominees who could serve as envoys, and Ruoshui was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong was about to send envoys to the Jin court to discuss redeeming the Three Prefectures with tax revenues. An edict called for men fit to serve as envoys, and Ruoshui was chosen.

sentences.zh: 召對，賜今名，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was granted his present name and promoted to Assistant Drafter in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was granted his present name and promoted to Assistant Drafter in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 為使，見粘罕於雲中。

translations.literal: As envoy he met Nianhan at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy he met Nianhan at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 才歸，兵已南下，復假徽猷閣學士，副馮澥以往。

translations.literal: He had barely returned when troops were already marching south; he was again lent the title of Academician of the Huaiyou Pavilion and went as deputy to Feng Li.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely returned when Jin troops were already marching south. He was again lent the title of Academician of the Huaiyou Pavilion and went as deputy to Feng Li.

sentences.zh: 甫次中牟，守河兵相驚以金兵至，左右謀取間道去，澥問「何如」？

translations.literal: Just as they halted at Zhongmou, the river-guard troops panicked one another with reports that Jin troops had arrived; those around them plotted to take a bypath away; Li asked, "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: When they halted at Zhongmou, the river-guard troops panicked one another with word that Jin forces had arrived. Those around them plotted to slip away by a side road. Li asked, "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 若水曰：「戍卒畏敵而潰，奈何效之，今正有死耳。」

translations.literal: Ruoshui said: "The garrison troops feared the enemy and broke—how can we imitate them? At present there is only death."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui said, "The garrison troops feared the enemy and broke. How can we copy them? All that remains is to die."

sentences.zh: 令敢言退者斬，眾乃定。

translations.literal: He ordered that anyone who dared speak of retreat be executed; the troops then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that anyone who spoke of retreat be executed, and the company steadied.

sentences.zh: 既行，疊具奏，言和議必不可諧，宜申飭守備。

translations.literal: Having set out, he repeatedly submitted memorials saying that peace negotiations could certainly not succeed and that defenses should be strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Once underway, he submitted memorial after memorial arguing that peace talks could not succeed and urging that defenses be tightened.

sentences.zh: 至懷州，遇館伴蕭慶，挾與俱還。

translations.literal: Reaching Huai Prefecture, he met the escort commissioner Xiao Qing, who forced him to return together.
translations.idiomatic: At Huai Prefecture he met the escort commissioner Xiao Qing, who forced him to turn back with him.

sentences.zh: 及都門，拘之於沖虛觀，獨令慶、澥入。

translations.literal: When they reached the capital gate, Ruoshui was detained at the Chongxu Abbey while only Qing and Li were allowed to enter.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital gate Ruoshui was detained at the Chongxu Abbey while only Qing and Li were admitted.

sentences.zh: 既所議多不從，粘罕急攻城，若水入見帝，道其語，帝命何㮚行。

translations.literal: Since most of what was discussed was not accepted, Nianhan pressed the siege urgently. Ruoshui entered to see the Emperor, relayed their words, and the Emperor ordered He Li to go.
translations.idiomatic: When most of what was negotiated was rejected, Nianhan pressed the siege hard. Ruoshui entered to see the emperor, reported their demands, and the emperor ordered He Li to go.

sentences.zh: 㮚還，言二人欲與上皇相見，帝曰：「朕當往。」

translations.literal: He returned saying the two men wished to meet the Retired Emperor. The Emperor said, "I shall go."
translations.idiomatic: He returned saying the two men wished to meet the Retired Emperor. The emperor said, "I shall go myself."

sentences.zh: 明日幸金營，過信而歸。

translations.literal: The next day he visited the Jin camp and, relying on their assurances, returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he visited the Jin camp and returned on their pledge of good faith.

sentences.zh: 擢若水禮部尚書，固辭。

translations.literal: Ruoshui was elevated to Minister of Rites but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui was promoted to Minister of Rites but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「學士與尚書同班，何必辭。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "An academician and a minister rank in the same court session—why must you decline?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "An academician and a minister sit in the same court session. Why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 請不已，改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He continued to petition without cease and was reassigned as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He kept petitioning without cease and was reassigned as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，金人再邀帝出郊，帝殊有難色，若水以為無他慮，扈從以行。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Jurchens again invited the Emperor to go outside the city; the Emperor showed considerable reluctance; Ruoshui, thinking there was no other concern, accompanied him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Jurchens again summoned the emperor outside the city. The emperor was deeply reluctant, but Ruoshui, seeing no other danger, accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 金人計中變，逼帝易服，若水抱持而哭，詆金人為狗輩。

translations.literal: The Jurchens' plot shifted midway; they forced the Emperor to change clothes; Ruoshui embraced and wept for him, denouncing the Jurchens as a pack of dogs.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens changed their plan midway and forced the emperor to change clothes. Ruoshui clung to him weeping and denounced the Jurchens as dogs.

sentences.zh: 金人曳出，擊之敗面，氣結僕地，眾皆散，留鐵騎數十守視。

translations.literal: The Jurchens dragged him out, struck him until his face was ruined; he lost breath and collapsed; the crowd all scattered; several tens of armored horsemen were left to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens dragged him out and beat his face to ruin. He lost breath and collapsed. The crowd scattered, and several dozen armored horsemen were left to watch him.

sentences.zh: 粘罕令曰：「必使李侍郎無恙。」

translations.literal: Nianhan ordered: "You must see that Vice Minister Li comes to no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan ordered, "See that Vice Minister Li comes to no harm."

sentences.zh: 若水絕不食，或勉之曰：「事無可為者，公昨雖言，國相無怒心，今日順從，明日富貴矣。」

translations.literal: Ruoshui absolutely refused to eat. Someone tried to encourage him: "There is nothing more to be done. Though you spoke harshly yesterday, the chief minister bears no anger. Submit today and tomorrow you will be rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui refused all food. Someone urged him, "Nothing more can be done. Though you spoke harshly yesterday, the chief minister bears no grudge. Yield today and tomorrow you will be rich and honored."

sentences.zh: 若水歎曰：「天無二日，若水寧有二主哉！」

translations.literal: Ruoshui sighed and said, "Heaven has but one sun—how could Ruoshui have two masters!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui sighed and said, "Heaven has but one sun. How could Ruoshui serve two masters?"

sentences.zh: 其僕亦來慰解曰：「公父母春秋高，若少屈，冀得一歸覲。」

translations.literal: His servant also came to comfort him: "Your lordship's parents are advanced in years; if you yield a little, you might hope to return once to visit them."
translations.idiomatic: His servant also tried to comfort him: "Your parents are old. If you yield a little, you may yet return to see them once."

sentences.zh: 若水叱之曰：「吾不復顧家矣！

translations.literal: Ruoshui rebuked him: "I no longer care for my family!
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui rebuked him: "I no longer care for my family!

sentences.zh: 忠臣事君，有死無二。

translations.literal: A loyal minister serves his ruler—with death there is no second choice.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister serves his ruler; in death there is no second master.

sentences.zh: 然吾親老，汝歸勿遽言，令兄弟徐言之可也。」

translations.literal: Yet my parents are old; when you return do not speak of this hastily—let my brothers tell them gradually."
translations.idiomatic: But my parents are old. When you return, do not tell them at once. Let my brothers break the news slowly."

sentences.zh: 後旬日，粘罕召計事，且問不肯立異姓狀。

translations.literal: More than ten days later, Nianhan summoned him to discuss affairs and also asked why he refused to sign the document naming a ruler of a different surname.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later Nianhan summoned him to discuss affairs and asked why he refused to sign the document installing a ruler of another surname.

sentences.zh: 若水曰：「上皇為生靈計，罪己內禪，主上仁孝慈儉，未有過行，豈宜輕議廢立？」

translations.literal: Ruoshui said, "The Retired Emperor, for the sake of the people, blamed himself and abdicated inwardly. Our sovereign is benevolent, filial, compassionate, and frugal, with no wrongful conduct—how can one lightly discuss deposing and installing?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui said, "The Retired Emperor, for the people's sake, blamed himself and abdicated. Our sovereign is benevolent, filial, compassionate, and frugal and has done no wrong. How can one lightly talk of deposing him?"

sentences.zh: 粘罕指宋朝失信，若水曰：「若以失信為過，公其尤也。」

translations.literal: Nianhan pointed to the Song's breach of faith. Ruoshui said, "If breach of faith is the fault, you above all are guilty."
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan accused the Song of breaking faith. Ruoshui said, "If breach of faith is the crime, you are guiltier than anyone."

sentences.zh: 歷數其五事曰：「汝為封豕長蛇，真一劇賊，滅亡無日矣。」

translations.literal: He enumerated five offenses and said, "You are a ravening hog and long serpent, a true arch-villain—your destruction is not far off."
translations.idiomatic: He listed five offenses and said, "You are a ravening hog and long serpent, a true arch-villain. Your ruin is not far off."

sentences.zh: 粘罕令擁之去，反顧罵益甚。

translations.literal: Nianhan ordered him dragged away; looking back he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan ordered him dragged away. Looking back, he cursed all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 至郊壇下，謂其僕謝寧曰：「我為國死，職耳，奈並累若屬何！」

translations.literal: Reaching the foot of the suburban altar, he said to his servant Xie Ning, "I die for the state—that is my duty; but how can I bear to drag you all down with me!"
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the suburban altar he said to his servant Xie Ning, "I die for the state—that is my duty. But how can I bear to drag you down with me?"

sentences.zh: 又罵不絕口，監軍者撾破其唇，噀血罵愈切，至以刃裂頸斷舌而死，年三十五。

translations.literal: Again he cursed without pause; the guards beat his lips apart; spewing blood he cursed all the more sharply; finally they slashed his neck and cut out his tongue, and he died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Again he cursed without pause. The guards beat his lips apart; spewing blood, he cursed all the sharper. At last they cut his neck and severed his tongue. He died at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 寧得歸，具言其狀。

translations.literal: Ning was able to return and recounted the whole affair in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Ning made it back and told the whole story in detail.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，下詔曰：「若水忠義之節，無與比倫，達于朕聞，為之涕泣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he issued an edict: "Ruoshui's loyal and righteous integrity is matchless; having learned of it, We are moved to tears."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he issued an edict: "Ruoshui's loyal and righteous integrity is beyond compare. Learning of it, We are moved to tears."

sentences.zh: 特贈觀文殿學士，諡曰忠湣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Academician of the Guanwen Hall, with the posthumous title Zhongmin (Loyal and Lamented).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Academician of the Guanwen Hall, with the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 死後有自北方逃歸者云：「金人相與言，'遼國之亡，死義者十數，南朝惟李侍郎一人'。

translations.literal: After his death, one who had escaped from the north reported: "The Jurchens said among themselves, 'When the Liao state fell, more than ten died for righteousness; in the Southern Court there is only Vice Minister Li alone.
translations.idiomatic: After his death a man who had escaped from the north reported, "The Jurchens said among themselves, 'When the Liao fell, more than ten died for righteousness. In the Southern Court there is only Vice Minister Li.

sentences.zh: 臨死無怖色，為歌詩卒，曰：'矯首問天兮，天卒無言，忠臣效死兮，死亦何愆？

translations.literal: Facing death he showed no look of fear and composed a poem in song before he died, saying: 'Raising my head I ask Heaven—Heaven at last is silent; a loyal minister gives his life—what fault in dying?'
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he showed no fear and composed a final song-poem: "Raising my head I ask Heaven—Heaven gives no answer. A loyal minister dies in service—what fault is there in death?"

sentences.zh: '聞者悲之。」

translations.literal: Those who heard it were grieved."
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it were deeply grieved."

sentences.zh: 劉韐，字仲偃，建州崇安人。

translations.literal: Liu Ge, style name Zhongyan, was a man of Chong'an in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ge, styled Zhongyan, was from Chong'an in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調豐城尉、隴城令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as commandant of Fengcheng and magistrate of Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed commandant of Fengcheng and magistrate of Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 王厚鎮熙州，辟狄道令，提舉陝西平貨司。

translations.literal: When Wang Hou governed Xizhou, Ge was recruited as magistrate of Didao and appointed supervisor of the Shaanxi Equitable-Price Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hou governed Xizhou, Ge was recruited as magistrate of Didao and appointed supervisor of the Shaanxi Equitable-Price Bureau.

sentences.zh: 河、湟兵屯多，食不繼，韐延致酋長，出金帛從易粟，就以餉軍，公私便之。

translations.literal: In the He and Huang regions many troops were encamped and food did not follow; Ge invited tribal chiefs, offered gold and silk to buy grain in exchange, and with it supplied the army—public and private interests alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Many troops were stationed along the He and Huang rivers and supplies ran short. Ge invited tribal chiefs, exchanged gold and silk for grain, and used it to feed the army, to the benefit of both public and private interests.

sentences.zh: 遂為轉運使，擢中大夫、集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: He then became transport commissioner and was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and Compiler in the Hall for Cultivating Talent.
translations.idiomatic: He then became transport commissioner and was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and Compiler in the Hall for Cultivating Talent.

sentences.zh: 劉法死，夏人攻震武。

translations.literal: When Liu Fa died, the Tangut attacked Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Fa died, the Tangut attacked Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 韐攝帥鄜延，出奇兵搗之，解其圍。

translations.literal: Ge acted as acting military commissioner of Fuyan, sent a surprise force to strike them, and raised the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Ge served as acting military commissioner of Fuyan, sent a surprise force against them, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 夏人來言，願納款謝罪，皆以為詐。

translations.literal: The Tangut sent word that they wished to submit and apologize; all thought it a ruse.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut sent word that they wished to submit and apologize, but all thought it a trick.

sentences.zh: 韐曰：「兵興累年，中國尚不支，況小邦乎？

translations.literal: Ge said, "War has gone on for years; China itself can barely sustain it—how much less a small state?
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "War has dragged on for years. China itself can barely sustain it—how much less a small state?

sentences.zh: 彼雖新勝，其眾亦疲，懼吾再舉，故款附以圖自安，此情實也。」

translations.literal: Though they have newly won, their forces are also weary; fearing we will strike again, they submit in friendship to seek their own security—this feeling is genuine."
translations.idiomatic: Though they have just won, their forces are weary too. Fearing we will strike again, they submit to secure themselves. That feeling is genuine."

sentences.zh: 密疏以聞，詔許之。

translations.literal: He reported this in a secret memorial and received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this in a secret memorial, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 夏使愆期不至，諸將言夏果詐，請會兵乘之。

translations.literal: The Tangut envoy missed the appointed date; the generals said the Tangut had indeed deceived them and asked to gather troops and seize the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut envoy missed the appointed date, the generals said the Tangut had indeed deceived them and asked to gather troops and strike.

sentences.zh: 韐曰：「越境約會，容有他故。」

translations.literal: Ge said, "Cross-border appointments may have other reasons for delay."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "Cross-border appointments may be delayed for other reasons."

sentences.zh: 會再請者至，韐戒曰：「朝廷方事討伐，吾為汝請，毋若異時邀歲幣，軼疆場，以取威怒。」

translations.literal: When the envoy who came to renew the request arrived, Ge warned: "The court is presently set on punitive campaigns; I have pleaded on your behalf—do not, as in times past, press for annual tribute payments, violate the border, and incur imperial wrath."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy who came to renew the request arrived, Ge warned, "The court is bent on punitive campaigns. I have pleaded for you. Do not, as before, press for annual tribute, violate the border, and invite imperial wrath."

sentences.zh: 夏人聽命，西邊自是遂安。

translations.literal: The Tangut obeyed, and from then on the western frontier was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut obeyed, and from then on the western frontier was at peace.

sentences.zh: 韐求東歸，拜徽猷閣待制，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Ge sought to return east and was appointed Chamberlain for Attendant Readiness of the Huaiyou Pavilion and Supervisor of the Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ge sought to return east and was appointed Chamberlain for Attendant Readiness of the Huaiyou Pavilion and Supervisor of the Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知越州，鑒湖為民侵耕，官因收其租，歲二萬斛。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as prefect of Yuezhou: Mirror Lake had been encroached upon by farmers for cultivation; the government accordingly collected rent on it, twenty thousand bushels per year.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as prefect of Yuezhou, he found that farmers had encroached on Mirror Lake for cultivation; the government collected rent on it, twenty thousand bushels a year.

sentences.zh: 政和間，涸以為田，衍至六倍，隸中宮應奉，租太重而督索嚴，多逃去。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era it was drained for fields, expanding to six times the original area, placed under the inner palace's tribute office; the rent was too heavy and collection enforcement severe, and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era the lake was drained for fields, expanding to six times its former area and placed under the inner palace tribute office. The rent was crushing and collection harsh, and many fled.

sentences.zh: 前勒鄰伍取償，民告病，韐請而蠲之。

translations.literal: Previously the authorities compelled neighboring households to make up the shortfall; the people complained of hardship; Ge petitioned and the levy was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the authorities had forced neighboring households to make up the shortfall. The people complained bitterly, and Ge petitioned to have the levy remitted.

sentences.zh: 方臘陷衢、婺，越大震，官吏悉遁，或具舟請行。

translations.literal: When Fang La took Qu and Wu, Yue was greatly shaken; officials all fled; some prepared boats and urged departure.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La took Qu and Wu, Yue was thrown into panic. Officials fled, and some prepared boats and urged him to leave.

sentences.zh: 韐曰：「吾為郡守，當與城存亡。」

translations.literal: Ge said, "I am prefect of this commandery—I should live or die with the city."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "I am prefect of this commandery. I should live or die with the city."

sentences.zh: 不為動，益厲戰守備。

translations.literal: He was unmoved and redoubled preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He would not budge and redoubled the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 寇至城下，擊敗之，拜述古殿直學士，召為河北、河東宣撫參謀官。

translations.literal: When bandits reached the city walls he defeated them; he was appointed Direct Academician of the Shugu Hall and summoned as staff officer to the Hebei and Hedong Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits reached the walls he defeated them. He was appointed Direct Academician of the Shugu Hall and summoned as staff officer to the Hebei and Hedong Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時邊臣言，燕民思內附，童貫、蔡攸方出師，而種師道之軍潰。

translations.literal: At the time frontier officials reported that the people of Yan wished to defect inward; Tong Guan and Cai You were just setting out on campaign when Zhong Shidao's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time frontier officials reported that the people of Yan wished to come over to the Song. Tong Guan and Cai You were just setting out when Zhong Shidao's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 韐意警報不實，見師道計事。

translations.literal: Ge suspected the alarm was unfounded and went to see Shidao to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ge suspected the alarm was false and went to consult Shidao.

sentences.zh: 師道曰：「契丹兵勢尚盛，而燕人未有應者，恐邊臣誕謾誤國事。」

translations.literal: Shidao said, "Khitan military strength is still formidable, yet the people of Yan have not responded—I fear frontier officials have lied and will ruin the state's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao said, "Khitan forces are still strong, yet the people of Yan have not risen. I fear frontier officials have lied and will ruin the state's business."

sentences.zh: 韐即馳白貫、攸，請班師。

translations.literal: Ge immediately galloped to inform Tong and You and requested withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ge immediately rode to inform Tong and You and asked that the army be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 又論燕薊不可得，正使得之，屯兵遣餉，經費無藝，必重困中國。

translations.literal: He also argued that Yan and Ji could not be taken; even if they were obtained, garrisoning troops and dispatching supplies would cost without limit and would surely gravely afflict China.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Yan and Ji could not be taken; even if they were, garrisoning troops and shipping supplies would cost without limit and would crush the empire.

sentences.zh: 還次莫州，會郭藥師以涿州降，戎車再駕，以韐議異，徙知真定府。

translations.literal: Returning, he halted at Mozhou; when Guo Yaoshi surrendered Zhuozhou, the war chariot set out again; because Ge's views differed, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he halted at Mozhou. When Guo Yaoshi surrendered Zhuozhou, the campaign set out again. Because Ge's views differed, he was transferred to prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 藥師入朝，韐密奏乞留之，不報。

translations.literal: When Yaoshi entered court, Ge secretly memorialized asking that he be detained; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoshi came to court, Ge secretly memorialized asking that he be detained. The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 徙知建州，改福州，加延康殿學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jianzhou, then Fuzhou, and granted Academician of the Yankang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jianzhou, then Fuzhou, and granted Academician of the Yankang Hall.

sentences.zh: 或言其過闕時，見御史中丞有所請，遂罷。

translations.literal: Someone reported that when passing through the palace gate he was seen making a request to the Censor-in-Chief, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that when passing through the palace gate he had been seen petitioning the Censor-in-Chief, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起知荊南，河北盜起，復以守真定。

translations.literal: Recalled to govern Jingnan; when bandits rose in Hebei, he was again put in charge of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Jingnan. When bandits rose in Hebei, he was again put in charge of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 首賊柴宏本富室，不堪征斂，聚眾剽奪，殺巡尉，統制官亦戰死。

translations.literal: The chief bandit Chai Hong had originally been a wealthy household, unable to bear the levies; he gathered a crowd to plunder, killed patrol officers, and a control officer also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The chief bandit Chai Hong had been a wealthy man who could not bear the levies. He gathered followers to plunder, killed patrol officers, and a control officer also died fighting him.

sentences.zh: 韐單騎赴鎮，遣招之，宏至服罪。

translations.literal: Ge rode alone to his post, sent to summon him; Hong came and submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ge rode alone to his post, sent to summon Hong, and Hong came to submit to punishment.

sentences.zh: 韐飲之酒，請以官，縱其黨還田裏，一路遂平。

translations.literal: Ge gave him wine, requested an office for him, released his followers to return to their villages, and the whole circuit was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ge gave him wine, asked that he be given an office, and released his followers to return to their villages. The whole circuit was pacified.

sentences.zh: 藥師請馬，詔盡以河北戰馬與之，不足，又賦諸民。

translations.literal: Yaoshi requested horses; an edict gave him all the war horses of Hebei; when these were insufficient, the levy was extended to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi requested horses. An edict gave him all the war horses of Hebei; when that was not enough, the levy was extended to the people.

sentences.zh: 韐曰：「空內郡駔駿，付一降將，非計也。」

translations.literal: Ge said, "To empty the inner commanderies of their thoroughbreds and hand them to a single surrendered general is no wise plan."
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "To strip the inner commanderies of their best horses and hand them to one surrendered general is no wise plan."

sentences.zh: 奏止之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 金人已謀南牧，朝廷方從之求雲中地。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were already plotting to drive south; the court was just then acceding to their request for the Yunzhong territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were already planning to drive south, even as the court was acceding to their request for the Yunzhong territory.

sentences.zh: 韐諜得實，急以聞，且陰治城守以待變。

translations.literal: Ge's spies obtained proof and he urgently reported it, while quietly strengthening the city's defenses to await whatever might come.
translations.idiomatic: Ge's spies confirmed it. He reported urgently and quietly strengthened the city's defenses to await whatever might come.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金兵抵城下，知有備，留兵其旁，長驅內向。

translations.literal: That winter, Jin troops reached the city walls; seeing it was prepared, they left troops nearby and drove straight inland.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Jin troops reached the walls. Seeing the city prepared, they left troops nearby and drove straight inland.

sentences.zh: 及還，治梯沖設圍，示欲攻擊，韐發強駑射之，金人知不可脅，乃退。

translations.literal: When they returned, they prepared scaling ladders and siege engines and set up encirclement, showing intent to attack; Ge deployed powerful crossbows and shot at them; the Jurchens knew they could not coerce him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned, they built scaling ladders and siege engines and set up a siege, feigning attack. Ge deployed powerful crossbows and shot at them. The Jurchens saw they could not force him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自金兵之來，諸郡皆塞門，民坐困，韐獨縱樵牧如平日，以時啟閉。

translations.literal: Since the Jin troops came, every commandery shut its gates and the people sat trapped; Ge alone let woodcutters and herdsmen go out as on ordinary days, opening and closing the gates on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin troops came, every commandery had shut its gates and the people were trapped indoors. Ge alone let woodcutters and herdsmen go out as on ordinary days, opening and closing the gates on schedule.

sentences.zh: 欽宗善之，拜資政殿學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong approved of this and appointed him Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong approved and appointed him Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 時已許割地賂金人，而議者乘士民之憤，復議追躡，韐以亟戰為非。

translations.literal: By then territory had already been promised to pay off the Jurchens, but those who debated the issue, riding the anger of soldiers and civilians, again proposed pursuit; Ge considered rushing to battle wrong.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already agreed to cede territory to buy off the Jurchens, but debaters, seizing on the anger of soldiers and civilians, again proposed hot pursuit. Ge held that rushing into battle was wrong.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸將救太原，種師中、姚古敗。

translations.literal: At this time the generals went to relieve Taiyuan; Zhong Shizhong and Yao Gu were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the generals marched to relieve Taiyuan. Zhong Shizhong and Yao Gu were defeated.

sentences.zh: 以韐為宣撫副使，至遼州，招集糾募，得兵四萬人，與解潛、折可求約期俱進，兩人又繼敗。

translations.literal: Ge was made Deputy Commissioner for Pacification; he reached Liaozhou, gathered and recruited troops, and obtained forty thousand men; he and Xie Qian and Zhe Keqiu set a date to advance together, but the two of them again suffered defeat in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was appointed Deputy Commissioner for Pacification. At Liaozhou he raised and mustered troops until he had forty thousand men. He arranged with Xie Qian and Zhe Keqiu to advance together on a fixed date, but both were defeated in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，韐遣別將賈瓊自代州出敵背，且許義軍以爵祿，得首領數十。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ge had sent the separate commander Jia Qiong out from Daizhou to strike the enemy's rear, and also promised ranks and stipends to the righteous armies, gaining several dozen chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ge had sent another commander, Jia Qiong, out from Daizhou to hit the enemy from the rear, and had promised ranks and stipends to militia leaders, winning over several dozen chieftains.

sentences.zh: 既復五台，而潛、可求敗聞，遂不果進。

translations.literal: After Wutai was recovered, but news arrived of defeats by Qian and Keqiu, they consequently did not carry through the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wutai was recovered, but when word came that Qian and Keqiu had been defeated, the advance was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 太原陷，召入覲，為京城四壁守禦使，宰相沮罷之。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan fell, he was summoned to court for an audience and made Defender of the Four Walls of the Capital; the chief councillors obstructed and had him removed from the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan fell he was summoned to court and appointed Defender of the Four Walls of the Capital, but the chief councillors blocked the appointment and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 韐莊重寬厚，與人交，若有畏者；

translations.literal: Ge was solemn, generous, and mild; in dealings with others he seemed one who inspired awe;
translations.idiomatic: Ge was grave, generous, and mild. In his dealings with others he seemed almost intimidating;

sentences.zh: 至臨大事則毅然不可回奪。

translations.literal: yet when faced with great affairs he was resolute and could not be turned aside.
translations.idiomatic: yet when great affairs were at stake he was resolute and could not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 初在西州為童貫所知，故首尾預其軍事，及以忠死，論者不復短其前失雲。

translations.literal: Early on in Xizhou he had been noticed by Tong Guan, and so from beginning to end he took part in his military affairs; when he died for loyalty, those who commented no longer spoke ill of his earlier faults.
translations.idiomatic: Early on in Xizhou he had caught Tong Guan's eye and so had been involved in his military campaigns from start to finish. When he died loyal to the state, commentators no longer dwelt on his earlier mistakes.

sentences.zh: 子子羽、孫珙，自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Ziyu and Gong have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Ziyu and Gong have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 傅察，字公晦，孟州濟源人，中書侍郎堯俞從孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Cha, styled Gonghui, was a native of Jiyuan in Meng Prefecture and a grand-nephew of Yaoyu, Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cha, styled Gonghui, was from Jiyuan in Meng Prefecture and a grand-nephew of Yaoyu, Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 年十八，登進士第。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 蔡京在相位，聞其名，遣子鯈往見，將妻以女，拒弗答。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing held the chancellorship, hearing his name he sent his son Chou to visit him, intending to give him his daughter in marriage; he refused and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was chancellor, he heard of Cha's reputation and sent his son Chou to visit him, intending to marry him to his daughter. Cha refused and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 調青州司法參軍，曆永平、淄川丞，入為太常博士，遷兵部、吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Assigned as judicial aide in Qing Prefecture, he served successively as assistant magistrate of Yongping and Zichuan, entered service as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministries of War and of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as judicial aide in Qing Prefecture, then served as assistant magistrate of Yongping and Zichuan. He entered the capital as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministries of War and of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年十月，接伴金國賀正旦使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Xuanhe, he served as escort commissioner for the Jin envoys coming to congratulate on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Xuanhe, he was appointed escort commissioner for the Jin envoys coming to congratulate the court on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 是時，金將渝盟，而朝廷未之知也。

translations.literal: At this time the Jin were about to break the alliance, but the court did not yet know it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Jin were about to break the alliance, but the court did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 察至燕，聞金人入寇，或勸毋遽行。

translations.literal: When Cha reached Yan, he heard the Jurchens were invading; some advised him not to hurry on.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha reached Yan, he heard that the Jurchens were invading. Some urged him not to press on.

sentences.zh: 察曰：「受使以出，聞難而止，若君命何。」

translations.literal: Cha said: "Having received a mission and set out, to stop upon hearing of trouble — what of the ruler's command?"
translations.idiomatic: Cha said, "Having received a mission and set out, to halt when one hears of danger — what becomes of the ruler's command?"

sentences.zh: 遂至韓城鎮。

translations.literal: So he went on to Hancheng town.
translations.idiomatic: So he continued on to Hancheng town.

sentences.zh: 使人不來，居數日，金數十騎馳入館，強之上馬，行次境上，察覺有變，不肯進，曰：「迓使人，故例止此。」

translations.literal: The envoys did not come; after several days, several dozen Jurchen horsemen galloped into the lodge and forced him onto a horse; when they reached the border, Cha sensed something amiss and refused to go farther, saying: "In receiving envoys, by precedent one stops here."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys never came. After several days, several dozen Jurchen horsemen galloped into the lodge and forced him onto a horse. When they reached the border, Cha sensed something was wrong and refused to go farther. "In escorting envoys," he said, "by precedent one stops here."

sentences.zh: 金人輒易其馭者，擁之東北去，行百里許，遇所謂二太子斡離不者領兵至驛道，使拜。

translations.literal: The Jurchens immediately changed his driver and escorted him northeast; after traveling about a hundred li, they met the so-called Second Prince, Wolibu, leading troops to the post road and ordered him to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens immediately changed his escort and marched him northeast. After about a hundred li they met the so-called Second Prince, Wolibu, leading troops on the post road, who ordered him to bow.

sentences.zh: 察曰：「吾若奉使大國，見國主當致敬，今來迎客而脅我至此！

translations.literal: Cha said: "If I were on a mission to a great state, I should pay respects when meeting the ruler; now I came to receive guests and you have coerced me here!
translations.idiomatic: Cha said, "If I were on a mission to a great state, I would pay respects when meeting the ruler. But I came to receive guests, and you have forced me here!

sentences.zh: 又止令見太子，太子雖貴人，臣也，當以賓禮見，何拜為？」

translations.literal: Moreover you only have me meet the prince; though the prince is a noble person, he is still a subject, and I should meet him with guest rites — why should I bow?"
translations.idiomatic: And you only require me to meet the prince. However exalted the prince may be, he is still a subject. I should meet him with the rites due a guest — why should I bow?"

sentences.zh: 斡離不怒曰：「吾興師南向，何使之稱？

translations.literal: Wolibu angrily said: "I have raised an army and marched south — what mission do you speak of?
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu said angrily, "I have raised an army and marched south. What mission do you speak of?

sentences.zh: 凡汝國得失，為我道之，否則死。」

translations.literal: Tell me all the gains and losses of your state, or die."
translations.idiomatic: Tell me everything about your state's strengths and weaknesses, or die."

sentences.zh: 察曰：「主上仁聖，與大國講好，信使往來，項背相望，未有失德。

translations.literal: Cha said: "Our sovereign is benevolent and sage; he has made peace with your great state, and envoys have come and gone one after another without any lapse in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Cha said, "Our sovereign is benevolent and sage. He has made peace with your great state, and envoys have traveled back and forth in an unbroken stream. There has been no lapse in virtue.

sentences.zh: 太子幹盟而動，意欲何為？

translations.literal: The prince breaks the alliance and takes action — what does he intend?
translations.idiomatic: The prince has broken the alliance and taken action. What does he intend?

sentences.zh: 還朝當具奏。」

translations.literal: When I return to court I shall report this in full."
translations.idiomatic: When I return to court I shall report this in full."

sentences.zh: 斡離不曰：「爾尚欲還朝邪！」

translations.literal: Wolibu said: "Do you still think you can return to court!"
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu said, "Do you still think you can return to court!"

sentences.zh: 左右促使拜，白刃如林，或捽之伏地，衣袂顛倒，愈植立不顧，反覆論辨。

translations.literal: Those at his sides urged him to bow; naked blades stood like a forest; some dragged him to the ground, his sleeves and hem turned upside down, yet he stood all the more upright and unheeding, arguing back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants pressed him to bow. Naked blades stood like a forest. Some dragged him to the ground until his sleeves and hem were turned upside down, yet he stood all the more upright and unyielding, arguing back and forth.

sentences.zh: 斡離不曰：「爾今不拜，後日雖欲拜，可得邪！」

translations.literal: Wolibu said: "If you do not bow today, even if you wish to bow later, will you be able to?"
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu said, "If you do not bow today, even if you wish to bow later, will you be able to?"

sentences.zh: 麾令去。

translations.literal: He waved his hand and ordered him taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He waved his hand and ordered him taken away.

sentences.zh: 察知不免，謂官屬侯彥等曰：「我死必矣，我父母素愛我，聞之必大戚。

translations.literal: Cha knew he could not escape and said to his staff members Hou Yan and others: "I am sure to die; my parents have always loved me, and when they hear of it they will be deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Cha knew he could not escape. He said to his staff members Hou Yan and others, "I am sure to die. My parents have always loved me, and when they hear of it they will be deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 若萬一脫，幸記吾言，告吾親，使知我死國，少紓其亡窮之悲也。」

translations.literal: If by any chance you escape, please remember my words and tell my parents, so that knowing I died for the state they may be a little eased in their boundless grief."
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance you escape, please remember what I say and tell my parents, so that knowing I died for the state they may find some relief from their boundless grief."

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 是夕隔絕，不復見。

translations.literal: That evening he was cut off and was never seen again.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he was cut off from them and was never seen again.

sentences.zh: 金兵至燕，彥等密訪存亡，曰：「使臣不拜太子，昨郭藥師戰勝有喜色，太子慮其劫取，且銜往忿，殺之矣。」

translations.literal: When the Jin troops reached Yan, Yan and the others secretly inquired whether he was alive or dead and were told: "The envoy refused to bow to the prince; yesterday Guo Yaoshi's victory put the prince in good humor, but the prince feared he would be seized in a rescue and, still nursing old resentment, had him killed."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin troops reached Yan, Yan and the others secretly inquired after him and were told, "The envoy refused to bow to the prince. Yesterday Guo Yaoshi's victory had put the prince in good humor, but the prince feared a rescue attempt and, still nursing old resentment, had him killed."

sentences.zh: 將官武漢英識其屍，焚之，裹其骨，命虎翼卒沙立負以歸。

translations.literal: The officer Wu Hanying identified his corpse, burned it, wrapped the bones, and ordered the Tiger Wing soldier Sha Li to carry them home.
translations.idiomatic: The officer Wu Hanying identified his corpse, cremated it, wrapped the bones, and ordered the Tiger Wing soldier Sha Li to carry them home.

sentences.zh: 立至涿州，金人得而系諸土室，凡兩月。

translations.literal: When Li reached Zhuozhou, the Jurchens captured him and confined him in an earthen cell for two months in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Li reached Zhuozhou, the Jurchens captured him and locked him in an earthen cell for two months.

sentences.zh: 伺守者怠，毀垣出，歸以骨付其家。

translations.literal: Watching for the guards to slacken, he broke through the wall and escaped, returned, and delivered the bones to Cha's family.
translations.idiomatic: When the guards slackened, he broke through the wall and escaped, returned home, and delivered the bones to Cha's family.

sentences.zh: 副使蔣噩及彥輩歸，皆能道察不屈狀，贈徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: The deputy commissioner Jiang E and Yan and the others returned and all could describe how Cha had refused to yield; he was posthumously granted Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Splendid Writings.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commissioner Jiang E, Yan, and the others returned and all could describe Cha's refusal to yield. He was posthumously granted the title Attendant Drafting in the Hall of Splendid Writings.

sentences.zh: 察自幼嗜學，同輩或邀與娛嬉，不肯就。

translations.literal: From youth Cha was devoted to learning; when peers invited him to join in amusement and play, he would not go.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cha was devoted to learning. When peers invited him to join in amusement and play, he would not go.

sentences.zh: 為文溫麗有典裁。

translations.literal: His writing was warm, elegant, and well measured.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was warm, elegant, and well measured.

sentences.zh: 平居恂恂然，無喜慍色，遇事若無所可否，非其意，崒然不可犯。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was modest and deferential, showing neither joy nor anger; in affairs he seemed to approve or disapprove of nothing, but when something was not to his mind he suddenly became unapproachable.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life he was modest and deferential, showing neither joy nor anger. In affairs he seemed to approve or disapprove of nothing, but when something went against his mind he suddenly became unapproachable.

sentences.zh: 恬于勢利，在京師，故人鼎貴，罕至其門，間一見，寒溫談笑而已。

translations.literal: He was indifferent to power and profit; in the capital, though old friends rose to great eminence, they rarely came to his door, and when he saw them once in a while it was only to exchange greetings and casual talk.
translations.idiomatic: He was indifferent to power and profit. In the capital, though old friends rose to great eminence, they rarely came to his door, and when he saw them once in a while it was only to exchange greetings and casual talk.

sentences.zh: 及倉卒徇義，犖犖如此，聞者哀而壯之，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Yet when in haste he gave his life for righteousness, he stood out so remarkably that those who heard were moved to sorrow and admiration; he was then thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when in haste he gave his life for righteousness, he stood out so remarkably that those who heard were moved to sorrow and admiration. He was thirty-seven at the time.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，賜諡曰忠肅。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era he was granted the posthumous title Zhongsu, "Loyal and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiandao era he was granted the posthumous title Zhongsu, "Loyal and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 楊震，字子發，代州崞人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhen, styled Zifa, was a native of Guo in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhen, styled Zifa, was from Guo in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 以弓馬絕倫為安邊巡檢。

translations.literal: Because his archery and horsemanship were unmatched, he was made frontier patrol inspector of Anbian.
translations.idiomatic: Because his archery and horsemanship were unmatched, he was made frontier patrol inspector of Anbian.

sentences.zh: 河東軍征臧底河，敵據山為城，下瞰官軍，諸將合兵城下，震率壯士拔劍先登，斬數百級，眾乘勝平之，上功第一。

translations.literal: When the Hedong army campaigned on the Zangdi River, the enemy held the mountain as a fortress and looked down on the government troops; the generals combined their forces below the fort, and Zhen led brave men, drawing swords to climb first; they cut down several hundred heads, the troops pressed the victory and leveled the place, and his merit was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hedong army campaigned on the Zangdi River, the enemy held a mountain as a fortress and looked down on the government troops. The generals combined their forces below the fort. Zhen led brave men, swords drawn, in the first assault. They cut down several hundred heads, the troops pressed the victory and took the place, and his merit was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 從折可存討方臘，自浙東轉擊至三界鎮，斬首八千級。

translations.literal: Following Zhe Kechun in the campaign against Fang La, he turned from eastern Zhe and struck through to Sanjie town, taking eight thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhe Kechun in the campaign against Fang La, he turned from eastern Zhe and fought through to Sanjie town, taking eight thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 追襲至黃岩，賊帥呂師囊扼斷頭之險拒守，下石肆擊，累日不得進。

translations.literal: Pursuing the attack to Huangyan, the bandit chief Lü Shinang held the Decapitated Head defile and blocked the way, rolling down stones in fierce assault; for many days they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the attack to Huangyan, the bandit chief Lü Shinang held the Decapitated Head defile and blocked the way, rolling down stones in fierce assault. For many days they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 可存問計，震請以輕兵緣山背上，憑高鼓噪發矢石，賊驚走，已復縱火自衛。

translations.literal: Kechun asked for a plan; Zhen requested light troops to climb along the mountain ridge, and from the heights raise shouts, shoot arrows, and hurl stones; the bandits fled in alarm, but then set fires to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kechun asked for a plan. Zhen proposed sending light troops along the mountain ridge to shout from the heights and rain down arrows and stones. The bandits fled in alarm, but then set fires to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 震身被重鎧，與麾下履火突入，生得師囊，及殺首領三十人，進秩五等。

translations.literal: Zhen himself wore heavy armor and, with his men, marched through the fire and broke in, capturing Shinang alive and also killing thirty chieftains; he was promoted five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen himself wore heavy armor and, with his men, marched through the fire and broke in. He captured Shinang alive and killed thirty chieftains. He was promoted five ranks.

sentences.zh: 還知麟州建寧砦。

translations.literal: On his return he was made prefect of Lin Prefecture and commander of Jianning Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed prefect of Lin Prefecture and commander of Jianning Fort.

sentences.zh: 父 宗閔

translations.literal: Father: Zongmin
translations.idiomatic: Father: Zongmin

sentences.zh: 初，契丹之亡，其將小䩴䩮西奔，招合雜羌十余萬，破豐州，攻麟府諸城郭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan state fell, its general Xiao Ni'an fled west, gathered more than a hundred thousand mixed Qiang tribesmen, captured Feng Prefecture, and attacked the walled towns of Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Khitan state fell, its general Xiao Ni'an fled west, gathered more than a hundred thousand mixed Qiang tribesmen, captured Feng Prefecture, and attacked the walled towns of Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 震父宗閔領本道兵馬屢摧敗之，俘其父母妻子。

translations.literal: Zhen's father Zongmin, leading the military forces of the circuit, repeatedly crushed and defeated him and captured his parents, wife, and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Zongmin, leading the military forces of the circuit, repeatedly crushed and defeated him and captured his parents, wife, and children.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年十月，太原陷，䩴䩮驅幽薊叛卒與夏人奚人圍建寧，扣壁語震曰：「汝父奪我居，破我兵，掩我骨肉，我忍死到今，急舉城降，當全汝軀命。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jingkang, when Taiyuan fell, Ni'an drove rebel soldiers from You and Ji together with Tangut and Xi troops to besiege Jianning, knocked on the wall and said to Zhen: "Your father seized my home, broke my army, and captured my kin; I have endured death until now — hurry and surrender the city, and I will spare your life."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Jingkang, when Taiyuan fell, Ni'an drove rebel soldiers from You and Ji together with Tangut and Xi troops to besiege Jianning. He knocked on the wall and said to Zhen, "Your father seized my home, broke my army, and captured my kin. I have endured until now — hurry and surrender the city, and I will spare your life."

sentences.zh: 時城中守兵不滿百，震與戰士約，斬一級賞若干，官帑竭，繼以家人服珥，吏士感激自奮。

translations.literal: At the time the defenders in the city numbered fewer than a hundred; Zhen made a pact with the warriors that each head cut off would earn a set reward; when the official treasury was exhausted, he continued with his family's clothing and earrings, and officials and soldiers were moved to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the defenders numbered fewer than a hundred. Zhen promised the warriors a set reward for each head cut off. When the official treasury was exhausted, he paid with his family's clothing and earrings. Officials and soldiers were moved to fight all the harder.

sentences.zh: 越旬，矢盡力乏，城不守，與子居中、執中力戰沒，閤門俱喪，唯長子存中從征河北獨免。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, arrows were spent and strength exhausted; the city could not be held; he and his sons Juzhong and Zhizhong fought fiercely and perished; the whole household was lost, and only the eldest son Cunzhong, campaigning in Hebei, alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days, arrows were spent and strength exhausted and the city could not be held. He and his sons Juzhong and Zhizhong fought fiercely and perished. The whole household was lost; only the eldest son Cunzhong, campaigning in Hebei, escaped.

sentences.zh: 明年，宗閔亦死事于長安。

translations.literal: The next year Zongmin also died in service at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zongmin also died in service at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 震時年四十四。

translations.literal: Zhen was then forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was forty-four at the time.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，詔贈武經郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, an edict posthumously granted him the rank of Gentleman for Military Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan, an edict posthumously granted him the rank of Gentleman for Military Classics.

sentences.zh: 存中貴，請於朝，諡曰恭毅。

translations.literal: When Cunzhong rose to eminence, he petitioned the court, and the posthumous title Gongyi, "Respectful and Resolute," was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Cunzhong rose to eminence, he petitioned the court, and the posthumous title Gongyi, "Respectful and Resolute," was granted.

sentences.zh: 張克戩

translations.literal: Zhang Kejian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kejian

sentences.zh: 張克戩，字德祥，侍中耆曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Kejian, styled Dexiang, was a great-grandson of Qi, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kejian, styled Dexiang, was a great-grandson of Qi, Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 第進士，曆河間令，知吳縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Hejian, and was prefect of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Hejian, and was prefect of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 吳為浙劇邑，民喜爭，大姓怙勢持官府。

translations.literal: Wu was a difficult county in Zhe; the people loved litigation, and great clans relied on power to dominate the magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was a difficult county in Zhe. The people loved litigation, and great clans relied on power to dominate the magistracy.

sentences.zh: 為令者踵故抑首，務為不生事、幸得去而已。

translations.literal: Those who served as magistrate followed precedent and bowed their heads, striving only not to make trouble and hoping merely to get away.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates followed precedent and bowed their heads, striving only not to make trouble and hoping merely to get away.

sentences.zh: 克戩一裁以法，奸猾屏氣，使者以狀聞，召拜衛尉丞。

translations.literal: Kejian judged everything by law; the cunning and slippery held their breath; the commissioner reported his conduct to the throne, and he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian judged everything by law. The cunning and slippery held their breath. The commissioner reported his conduct to the throne, and he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，克戩從弟克公為御史，劾蔡京。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kejian's cousin Ke Gong had served as censor and impeached Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kejian's cousin Ke Gong had served as censor and impeached Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 京再輔政，修怨于張氏，以微事黜克戩。

translations.literal: When Jing again held power, he nursed a grudge against the Zhang clan and dismissed Kejian on a trivial matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing again held power, he nursed a grudge against the Zhang clan and dismissed Kejian on a trivial matter.

sentences.zh: 逾年，起知祥符縣，司開封戶曹，提舉京東常平，入辭，留為庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was reappointed prefect of Xiangfu County, served as clerk of household accounts in Kaifeng, was commissioner for the Eastern Capital Circuit's Ever-Normal Granaries, and when he came to take leave of the throne was retained as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was reappointed prefect of Xiangfu County, served as clerk of household accounts in Kaifeng, and was commissioner for the Eastern Capital Circuit's Ever-Normal Granaries. When he came to take leave of the throne he was retained as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年八月，知汾州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year of Xuanhe, he was made prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year of Xuanhe, he was appointed prefect of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，金兵犯河東，圍太原。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jin troops invaded Hedong and besieged Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jin troops invaded Hedong and besieged Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太原距汾二百里，遣將銀朱孛堇來攻，縱兵四掠，克戩畢力扞禦。

translations.literal: Taiyuan was two hundred li from Fen; the Jin sent the general Yinzhu Beijin to attack, letting his troops plunder on all sides; Kejian exerted all his strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan was two hundred li from Fen. The Jin sent the general Yinzhu Beijin to attack, letting his troops plunder on all sides. Kejian exerted all his strength in defense.

sentences.zh: 燕人先內附在城下者數十，陰結黨欲為內應，悉收斬之。

translations.literal: Several dozen men from Yan who had earlier submitted and were below the walls secretly formed a faction intending to serve as inside collaborators; he arrested and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen men from Yan who had earlier submitted and were below the walls secretly formed a faction intending to serve as inside collaborators. He arrested and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 數選勁卒撓敵營，出不意焚其柵，敵懼引去，論功加直秘閣。

translations.literal: Several times he selected crack troops to harass the enemy camp and, catching them off guard, burned their palisades; the enemy, fearing this, withdrew; for his merit he was promoted to Direct Associate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Several times he selected crack troops to harass the enemy camp and, catching them off guard, burned their palisades. The enemy, fearing this, withdrew. For his merit he was promoted to Direct Associate of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年六月，金兵復逼城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Jingkang, Jin troops again pressed the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Jingkang, Jin troops again pressed the city.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命經略使張孝純之子灝、都統制張思正、轉運使李宗來援，思正誅求無藝，民不堪命。

translations.literal: The court ordered the pacification commissioner Zhang Xiaochun's son Hao, the overall commander Zhang Sizheng, and the transport commissioner Li Zong to come to the rescue; Sizheng extorted without limit, and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the pacification commissioner Zhang Xiaochun's son Hao, the overall commander Zhang Sizheng, and the transport commissioner Li Zong to come to the rescue. Sizheng extorted without limit, and the people could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 克戩引誼開曉，皆願自奮。

translations.literal: Kejian appealed to their sense of duty and reasoned with them, and all were willing to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian appealed to their sense of duty and reasoned with them, and all were willing to fight harder.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使李綱表其守城之勞，連進直龍圖閣、右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: The Commissioner for Pacification Li Gang memorialized his labors in defending the city, and he was promoted in succession to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Compiler at the Hall of Right Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner for Pacification Li Gang memorialized his labors in defending the city, and he was promoted in succession to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Compiler at the Hall of Right Culture.

sentences.zh: 太原不守，思正紿雲出戰，遂率灝、宗奔慈、隰，於是人無固志。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan could not be held, Sizheng deceived them saying he would go out to battle, then led Hao and Zong in flight to Ci and Xi; after this the people had no firm will to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan could not be held, Sizheng deceived them saying he would go out to battle, then led Hao and Zong in flight to Ci and Xi. After this the people had no firm will to resist.

sentences.zh: 戍將麻世堅中夜斬關出，通判韓琥相繼亡，克戩召令兵民曰：「太原既陷，吾固知亡矣。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Ma Shijian cut through the gate and fled in the middle of the night; the vice prefect Han Hu likewise fled in succession; Kejian summoned the soldiers and civilians and said: "Now that Taiyuan has fallen, I already know we are doomed.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Ma Shijian cut through the gate and fled in the middle of the night. The vice prefect Han Hu likewise fled. Kejian summoned the soldiers and civilians and said, "Now that Taiyuan has fallen, I already know we are doomed.

sentences.zh: 然義不忍負國家、辱父祖，願與此城終始以明吾節，諸君其自為謀。」

translations.literal: Yet in righteousness I cannot bear to fail the state or disgrace my fathers and ancestors; I wish to see this city through to the end to make clear my integrity — you all must look to your own plans."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in righteousness I cannot bear to fail the state or disgrace my fathers and ancestors. I wish to see this city through to the end to make clear my integrity. You all must look to your own plans."

sentences.zh: 皆泣不能仰視，同辭而對曰：「公父母也，願盡死聽命。」

translations.literal: All wept and could not raise their eyes to look; with one voice they replied: "You are our father and mother; we wish to die to the last man and obey your command."
translations.idiomatic: All wept and could not raise their eyes to look. With one voice they replied, "You are our father and mother. We wish to die to the last man and obey your command."

sentences.zh: 乃益厲兵儆守。

translations.literal: Then he redoubled the drilling of troops and tightened the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Then he redoubled the drilling of troops and tightened the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊至，身帥將士擐甲登陴，雖屢卻敵而援師訖不至。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, he personally led the officers and soldiers, armored, onto the battlements; though they repeatedly repelled the enemy, relief troops never came.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived, he personally led the officers and soldiers, armored, onto the battlements. Though they repeatedly repelled the enemy, relief troops never came.

sentences.zh: 金兵破平遙，平遙為汾大邑，久與賊抗，既先陷，又脅降介休、孝義諸縣，據州南二十村，作攻城器具，兩遣使持書諭克戩，焚不啟。

translations.literal: Jin troops captured Pingyao; Pingyao was a great town of Fen and had long resisted the enemy; after it fell first, they also coerced Jiexiu, Xiaoyi, and other counties to surrender, occupied twenty villages south of the prefecture, made siege engines, and twice sent envoys bearing letters to instruct Kejian; he burned them unread.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops captured Pingyao. Pingyao was a great town of Fen and had long resisted the enemy. After it fell first, they also coerced Jiexiu, Xiaoyi, and other counties to surrender, occupied twenty villages south of the prefecture, and made siege engines. Twice they sent envoys bearing letters to instruct Kejian. He burned them unread.

sentences.zh: 具述危苦之狀，募士間道言之朝，不報。

translations.literal: He set forth in full the desperate plight, recruited men to go by hidden routes and report to the court, and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth in full the desperate plight and recruited men to go by hidden routes and report to the court. He received no reply.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，金益萬騎來攻愈急，有十人唱為降語，斬以徇。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, the Jin added ten thousand horsemen and pressed the attack ever harder; ten men were heard advocating surrender, and he executed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month, the Jin added ten thousand horsemen and pressed the attack ever harder. Ten men were heard advocating surrender, and he executed them as a warning.

sentences.zh: 諸酋列城下，克戩臨罵極口，炮中一酋，立斃。

translations.literal: The chieftains lined up below the wall; Kejian leaned over and cursed them to the full; a cannon shot struck one chieftain and killed him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains lined up below the wall. Kejian leaned over and cursed them to the full. A cannon shot struck one chieftain and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 度不得免，手草遺表及與妻子遺書，縋州兵持抵京師。

translations.literal: Judging that he could not escape, he personally drafted a final memorial and letters of farewell to his wife and children, and had a soldier of the prefecture lowered by rope to carry them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that he could not escape, he personally drafted a final memorial and letters of farewell to his wife and children, and had a soldier of the prefecture lowered by rope to carry them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明日，金兵從西北隅入，殺都監賈亶，克戩猶帥眾巷戰，金人募生致之。

translations.literal: The next day Jin troops entered from the northwest corner and killed the overseer Jia Dan; Kejian still led the crowd in street fighting; the Jurchens offered a reward to capture him alive.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jin troops entered from the northwest corner and killed the overseer Jia Dan. Kejian still led the crowd in street fighting. The Jurchens offered a reward to capture him alive.

sentences.zh: 克戩歸索朝服，焚香南向拜舞，自引決，一家死者八人。

translations.literal: Kejian returned home, asked for his court robes, burned incense and bowed facing south, and took his own life; eight members of his household died.
translations.idiomatic: Kejian returned home, asked for his court robes, burned incense and bowed facing south, and took his own life. Eight members of his household died.

sentences.zh: 金將奉其屍禮葬於後園，羅拜設祭，為立廟。

translations.literal: The Jin general had his corpse buried with ceremony in the rear garden, bowed in array and set out offerings, and had a temple built for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general had his corpse buried with ceremony in the rear garden, bowed in array and set out offerings, and had a temple built for him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔贈延康殿學士，贈銀三百兩、絹五百匹，表揭門閭。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict posthumously granted him Academician of the Hall for Extended Health, three hundred taels of silver and five hundred bolts of silk, and a memorial tablet posted at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, an edict posthumously granted him Academician of the Hall for Extended Health, three hundred taels of silver and five hundred bolts of silk, and a memorial tablet posted at his gate.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，諡忠確。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era he was granted the posthumous title Zhongque, "Loyal and Steadfast."
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaoxing era he was granted the posthumous title Zhongque, "Loyal and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 張確，字子固，邠州宜祿人。

translations.literal: Zhang Que, styled Ziggu, was a native of Yilu in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Que, styled Ziggu, was a native of Yilu in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，擢進士第。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era, he was elevated to jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，應詔上書言十事，乞誅大奸，退小人，進賢能，開禁錮，起老成，擢忠鯁，息邊事，修文德，廣言路，容直諫，遂列於上籍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, in response to an imperial call he submitted a memorial setting forth ten matters, begging to execute great villains, dismiss petty men, advance the worthy and capable, open the bans on office, recall the seasoned and mature, promote the loyal and outspoken, ease border affairs, cultivate civil virtue, broaden the channels of speech, and allow frank remonstrance; he was thereupon enrolled on the upper register.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, he responded to an imperial summons with a memorial outlining ten proposals: execute the greatest villains, dismiss petty officials, promote the worthy and capable, lift bans on office, recall seasoned statesmen, elevate the loyal and outspoken, reduce border tensions, restore civil virtue, broaden avenues for remonstrance, and welcome frank counsel. He was thereupon enrolled on the upper register.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，召至京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe, he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 青溪盜起，確言：「此皆王民，但庸人擾之耳。

translations.literal: When the Qingxi bandits rose, Que said: "These are all subjects of the king; it is only mediocre men who are disturbing them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qingxi bandits rose, Que said, "These are all the emperor's subjects—it is only incompetent officials who have stirred them up.

sentences.zh: 願下哀痛之詔，省不急之務，租賦之外，一切寢罷，敢以花石淫巧供上者死。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict of compassion and remorse be issued, non-urgent matters be curtailed, and everything beyond rents and taxes be abolished; those who dare supply the court with fancy stones and lavish curiosities shall die.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict of remorse and compassion, cut back non-urgent affairs, and abolish every levy beyond rents and taxes; let death be the penalty for anyone who dares furnish the court with ornamental stones and extravagant luxuries.

sentences.zh: 撫綏脅附，毋以多殺為功，旬浹之間，可以殄滅。」

translations.literal: Pacify and reassure those coerced into joining; do not take mass killing as merit; within ten days they can be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Pacify those who were forced to join, and do not treat slaughter as achievement—in ten days the rebels can be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 忤王黼意，通判杭州，攝睦州事。

translations.literal: Offending Wang Fu's wishes, he was made vice-prefect of Hangzhou and was charged with overseeing Muzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This offended Wang Fu, and he was made vice-prefect of Hangzhou with responsibility for Muzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 有自賊中逃歸者，悉宥之，訪得虛實以告，諸將用其言。

translations.literal: Those who escaped and returned from among the bandits were all pardoned; he investigated and learned what was true and false and reported it, and the generals followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned everyone who fled back from the rebels, investigated to learn what was true and what was false, and reported his findings; the generals acted on his counsel.

sentences.zh: 盜平，知坊、汾二州。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was made prefect of Fang and Fen Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was appointed prefect of Fang and Fen Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，徙解州，又徙隆德府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe, he was transferred to Jie Prefecture, then again to Longde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuanhe, he was transferred to Jie Prefecture and then to Longde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金兵圍太原，忻、代降，平陽兵叛。

translations.literal: Jin troops besieged Taiyuan; Xin and Dai surrendered, and the troops at Pingyang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops besieged Taiyuan; Xin and Dai surrendered, and the garrison at Pingyang mutinied.

sentences.zh: 確表言：「河東天下根本，安危所系，無河東，豈特秦不可守，汴亦不可都矣。

translations.literal: Que submitted a memorial stating: "Hedong is the foundation of the empire, to which safety and peril are bound; without Hedong, not only would Qin be indefensible—the capital at Bian would also be untenable.
translations.idiomatic: Que submitted a memorial stating, "Hedong is the empire's foundation and the pivot of its safety and peril. Without Hedong, not only would Qin be impossible to hold—even Bian could not remain the capital.

sentences.zh: 敵既得叛卒，勢必南下，潞城百年不修築，將兵又皆戍邊。

translations.literal: Once the enemy obtains the rebel troops, they will surely move south; Lucheng has gone a hundred years without repair, and the officers and troops are all garrisoned on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy takes the mutinous troops, they will surely push south. Lucheng has gone unrepaired for a century, and its officers and soldiers are all posted on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣生長西州，頗諳武事，若得秦兵十萬人，猶足以抗敵，不然，唯有一死報陛下耳。」

translations.literal: Your subject grew up in the western regions and is fairly versed in military affairs; if I am given a hundred thousand Qin troops, they would still suffice to resist the enemy; otherwise, I have only death with which to repay Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject was raised in the western regions and knows something of military affairs. Give me a hundred thousand Qin troops and I can still hold the enemy at bay; otherwise I have only my death to offer Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 書累上不報。

translations.literal: His memorials submitted repeatedly received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial, but none received a reply.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，金兵至，知城中無備，諭使降。

translations.literal: The following year in the second month, Jin troops arrived; knowing the city was unprepared, they urged him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the second month, Jin troops arrived. Seeing that the city was undefended, they urged him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 確乘城拒守，或獻謀欲自東城潰圍出，且探確意。

translations.literal: Que mounted the walls to resist; someone offered a plan to break out through the eastern wall, and also probed Que's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Que mounted the walls to resist the siege. Someone proposed breaking out through the eastern gate and tested Que's reaction.

sentences.zh: 確怒叱曰：「確守土臣，當以死報國，頭可斷，腰不可屈。」

translations.literal: Que angrily rebuked him, saying: "Que is a minister who holds the land; I should repay the state with my death—my head may be severed, but my waist will not bend."
translations.idiomatic: Que angrily rebuked him: "I am a minister charged with this land. I owe the state my death—my head may be cut off, but my back will not bow."

sentences.zh: 乃戰而死。

translations.literal: He then fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought and died.

sentences.zh: 欽宗聞之悲悼，優贈述古殿直學士，召見其子乂，慰撫之曰：「卿父今之巡、遠也，得其死所矣，復何恨。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong, hearing of it, grieved and mourned; he generously posthumously granted him Direct Academician of the Hall for Venerating Antiquity, summoned his son Yi, and comforted him, saying: "Your father is today's Xun and Yuan; he found the place to die—what regret could there be?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong heard the news, he grieved deeply. He posthumously granted Que the title of Direct Academician of the Hall for Venerating Antiquity, summoned his son Yi, and comforted him, saying, "Your father is this age's Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan. He found the death he sought—what more could he have wished for?

sentences.zh: 使為將為守者皆如卿父，朕顧有今日邪！」

translations.literal: If every general and defender were like your father, would I have today?"
translations.idiomatic: If every general and every defender were like your father, would I be in the plight I face today?"

sentences.zh: 斂容歎息者久之。

translations.literal: He composed his expression and sighed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He composed his face and sighed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 朱昭，字彥明，府穀人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhao, styled Yanming, was a native of Fugu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhao, styled Yanming, was a native of Fugu.

sentences.zh: 以效用進，累官秉義郎，浮湛班行，不自表異。

translations.literal: He advanced through military service, cumulatively reaching Bearer of Righteousness; he drifted among the ranks without distinguishing himself.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through military service, eventually reaching the rank of Bearer of Righteousness. He drifted unobtrusively through the ranks and never sought to stand out.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，為震威城兵馬監押，攝知城事。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, he was supervisor of troops and horses at Zhenwei Fort and was charged with overseeing the fort's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, he served as supervisor of troops and horses at Zhenwei Fort and was put in charge of the fort's affairs.

sentences.zh: 金兵內侵，夏人乘虛盡取河外諸城鎮。

translations.literal: Jin troops invaded inland, and the Tangut took advantage of the opening to seize all the forts and towns beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin troops invaded the interior, the Tangut seized the opportunity and took every fort and town west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 震威距府州三百里，最為孤絕。

translations.literal: Zhenwei was three hundred li from Fuzhou and was the most isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwei lay three hundred li from Fuzhou and was the most isolated of all.

sentences.zh: 昭率老幼嬰城，敵攻之力，昭募驍銳兵卒千餘人，與約曰：「賊知城中虛實，有輕我心，若出不意攻之，可一鼓而潰。」

translations.literal: Zhao led old and young into the city to defend it; as the enemy pressed the attack, Zhao recruited more than a thousand elite vigorous soldiers and pledged to them: "The bandits know the real situation inside the city and hold us in contempt; if we strike where they do not expect, we can rout them in one assault."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao led the old and young into the fort to hold it. As the enemy pressed the attack, he recruited more than a thousand of his best troops and pledged to them, "The enemy knows our strength inside the walls and looks down on us. Strike where they do not expect, and we can rout them in a single assault."

sentences.zh: 於是夜縋兵出，薄其營，果驚亂，城上鼓噪乘之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Accordingly, at night he lowered troops by rope to go out, pressed close to their camp, and they were indeed thrown into panic; those on the walls beat drums and shouted as they took advantage, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: That night he lowered troops over the wall by rope, closed on the enemy camp, and threw them into panic. Those on the walls beat drums and raised a clamor to press the advantage, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 夏人設木鵝梯沖以臨城，飛矢雨激，卒不能施，然晝夜進攻不止。

translations.literal: The Tangut set up wooden geese, scaling ladders, and battering rams against the city; arrows flew like rain and they could not be deployed, yet day and night the assault did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut raised siege towers, scaling ladders, and battering rams against the walls. Arrows fell like rain and the engines could not be brought to bear, yet the assault continued day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 其酋悟兒思齊介胄來，以氈盾自蔽，邀昭計事。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Wusiqi came in armor, shielding himself with felt shields, and invited Zhao to discuss matters.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Wusiqi came in armor, hiding behind felt shields, and asked to parley with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭常服登陴，披襟問曰：「彼何人，乃爾不武！

translations.literal: Zhao, in ordinary dress, mounted the ramparts, opened his collar, and asked: "Who is that man, so unmartial!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, in ordinary dress, mounted the ramparts, opened his collar, and called out, "Who is that—so timid in war!

sentences.zh: 欲見我，我在此，將有何事？」

translations.literal: If you wish to see me, I am here—what business do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: If you wanted to see me, here I am. What do you want?"

sentences.zh: 思齊卻盾而前，數宋朝失信，曰：「大金約我夾攻京師，為城下之盟，畫河為界；

translations.literal: Wusiqi put aside his shield and came forward, recounting the Song's broken faith, saying: "Great Jin agreed with us to attack the capital together; we made a treaty beneath the walls and drew the river as the boundary;
translations.idiomatic: Wusiqi lowered his shield and stepped forward, reciting the Song's broken promises: "Great Jin made a pact with us to attack the capital together. We swore a treaty beneath the walls and drew the river as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 太原旦暮且下，麟府諸壘悉已歸我，公何恃而不降？」

translations.literal: Taiyuan will fall any day now, and all the fortresses of Lin and Fu have already come over to us—what do you rely on in refusing to surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan will fall any day. Every fortress in Lin and Fu has already submitted to us. On what do you rely in refusing to surrender?"

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「上皇知奸邪誤國，改過不吝，已行內禪，今天子聖政一新矣，汝獨未知邪？」

translations.literal: Zhao said: "The Retired Emperor knows that villainy led the state astray, and he has not begrudged reform; he has already abdicated in favor of a successor, and today the Son of Heaven's virtuous governance is wholly renewed—do you alone not know this?"
