translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "The Retired Emperor knows that wicked men led the state astray and has not hesitated to reform. He has already abdicated in favor of a successor, and the Son of Heaven's governance is wholly renewed. Are you alone ignorant of this?"

sentences.zh: 乃取傳禪詔赦宣讀之，眾愕眙，服其勇辯。

translations.literal: He then took out the abdication edict and pardon and read them aloud; the crowd stared in astonishment and admired his bold eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the abdication edict and the general pardon and read them aloud. The crowd stared in astonishment and admired his courage and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸城降者多，昭故人從旁語曰：「天下事已矣，忠安所施？」

translations.literal: At this time many forts had surrendered; an old acquaintance of Zhao spoke from the side: "The affairs of the empire are already finished—where can loyalty be applied?"
translations.idiomatic: By then many forts had already surrendered. An old acquaintance of Zhao spoke up from the side: "The empire is finished. Where is there left to show loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 昭叱曰：「汝輩背義偷生，不異犬彘，尚敢以言誘我乎？

translations.literal: Zhao rebuked him: "You who betray righteousness to cling to life are no different from dogs and swine—how dare you try to entice me with words?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rebuked him: "You betray your duty to cling to life—you are no better than dogs and swine. How dare you try to tempt me with such talk?

sentences.zh: 我唯有死耳！」

translations.literal: I have only death!"
translations.idiomatic: I have only death!"

sentences.zh: 因大罵引弓射之，眾走。

translations.literal: He then cursed loudly, drew his bow, and shot at them; the crowd fled.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them loudly, drew his bow, and shot at them, and the crowd fled.

sentences.zh: 凡被圍四日，城多圮壞，昭以智補禦，皆合法，然不可復支。

translations.literal: In all they were besieged four days; much of the wall had collapsed, and Zhao used clever measures to reinforce the defense—all were sound in method, yet it could no longer be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted four days in all. Much of the wall had collapsed, and Zhao used every clever expedient to shore up the defense—all sound in method—yet the fort could no longer hold.

sentences.zh: 昭退坐廳事，召諸校謂曰：「城且破，妻子不可為賊汙，幸先戕我家而背城死戰，勝則東向圖大功，不勝則暴骨境內，大丈夫一生之事畢矣。」

translations.literal: Zhao withdrew and sat in the hall, summoned the officers, and said: "The city is about to fall; wives and children must not be defiled by bandits—would you first slay my household, then fight to the death with our backs to the wall? If we win, we shall turn east to achieve great deeds; if we lose, our bones will lie exposed within the territory—the business of a great man for one lifetime will be complete."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao withdrew to the hall, summoned his officers, and said, "The fort is about to fall. Our wives and children must not be defiled by the enemy. First slay my family, then let us fight to the death with our backs to the wall. If we win, we turn east and win great glory; if we lose, our bones will lie exposed within these borders. A man's whole life's business will then be complete."

sentences.zh: 眾未應。

translations.literal: The crowd did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 昭幼子戲階下，遽起手刃之，長子驚視，又殺之，徑領數卒屠其家人，舁屍納井中。

translations.literal: Zhao's youngest son was playing beneath the steps; he suddenly rose and killed him with his own hand; the eldest son looked up in shock and he killed him too; he directly led several soldiers to slaughter his household, lifted the corpses and put them in a well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's youngest son was playing on the steps below. Zhao suddenly rose and killed him with his own hand. His eldest son looked up in shock and Zhao killed him too. He then led several soldiers to slaughter the rest of his household, lifted the corpses, and cast them into a well.

sentences.zh: 部將賈宗望母適過前，昭起呼曰：「媼，鄉人也，吾不欲刃，請自入井。」

translations.literal: The deputy commander Jia Zongwang's mother happened to pass in front; Zhao rose and called out: "Old lady, you are from my home district—I do not wish to use the blade; please enter the well yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Jia Zongwang's mother happened to pass by. Zhao rose and called out, "Old lady, you are from my home district. I do not wish to use the blade on you—please throw yourself into the well."

sentences.zh: 媼從之，遂並覆以土。

translations.literal: The old lady complied, and they then covered everything with earth.
translations.idiomatic: The old lady complied, and they covered the well with earth.

sentences.zh: 將士將妻孥者，又皆盡殺之。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers who had wives and children also all killed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers who had wives and children killed them all as well.

sentences.zh: 昭謂眾曰：「我與汝曹俱無累矣！」

translations.literal: Zhao said to the crowd: "You and I are all unburdened now!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said to the men, "You and I are free of all encumbrances now!"

sentences.zh: 部落子有陰與賊通者，告之曰：「朱昭與其徒各殺其家人，將出戰，人雖少，皆死士也。」

translations.literal: A tribesman who had secretly communicated with the bandits reported: "Zhu Zhao and his men have each killed their own families and are about to go out to fight; though few in number, they are all men who will die."
translations.idiomatic: A tribesman who had secretly colluded with the enemy reported, "Zhu Zhao and his men have each killed their own families and are about to sally forth. They are few, but every one of them is a man ready to die."

sentences.zh: 賊大懼，以利啖守兵，得登城。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly afraid; they bribed the defending soldiers with profit and were able to mount the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was terrified. They bribed the garrison with rewards and were able to scale the walls.

sentences.zh: 昭勒眾于通衢接戰，自暮達旦，屍填街不可行。

translations.literal: Zhao rallied the crowd to fight in the main thoroughfare; from dusk until dawn corpses filled the street and it could not be traversed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rallied his men to fight in the main street. From dusk until dawn corpses filled the road until it could not be crossed.

sentences.zh: 昭躍馬從缺城出，馬蹶墜塹，賊歡曰：「得朱將軍矣！」

translations.literal: Zhao leaped on a horse and went out through a breach in the wall; the horse stumbled and fell into the ditch; the bandits rejoiced: "We have got General Zhu!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao leaped onto a horse and rode out through a breach in the wall. The horse stumbled and fell into the ditch. The enemy exulted, "We have got General Zhu!"

sentences.zh: 欲生致之。

translations.literal: They wished to capture him alive.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to take him alive.

sentences.zh: 昭瞋目仗劍，無一敢前，旋中矢而死，年四十六。

translations.literal: Zhao glared, sword in hand, and not one dared advance; presently he was struck by an arrow and died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao glared, sword in hand, and not one dared approach. Presently he was struck by an arrow and died. He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 史抗，濟源人。

translations.literal: Shi Kang, a native of Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kang was a native of Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，為代州沿邊安撫副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, he was deputy commissioner for frontier pacification of Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, he served as deputy commissioner for frontier pacification of Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人圍代急，抗夜呼其二子稽古、稽哲謂曰：「吾昔語用事者，'雁門控制一道，宜擇帥增戍以謀未形之患，若使橫流，則無所措矣'。

translations.literal: The Jurchens urgently besieged Dai; Kang called his two sons Jigu and Jizhe at night and said: "I once told those in power, 'Yanmen controls an entire route; one should choose a commander and increase garrisons to guard against trouble before it takes shape—if it is allowed to flood unchecked, there will be nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pressed the siege of Dai hard. Kang called his two sons, Jigu and Jizhe, to him at night and said, "I once told those in power, 'Yanmen controls an entire frontier route. Choose a capable commander, strengthen the garrisons, and guard against trouble before it takes shape. If disaster is allowed to flood unchecked, there will be nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 言雖切，皆不吾省。

translations.literal: Though my words were urgent, none gave heed to me.
translations.idiomatic: My words were urgent, but no one paid me any heed.

sentences.zh: 今重圍既固，外援不至，吾用六壬術占之，明日城必陷，吾將死事，汝輩亦勿以妻子為念而負國也。

translations.literal: Now the tight siege is already firm and outside aid does not come; I have divined by the Liuren method—the city will fall tomorrow; I shall die in service to the state; you too must not let concern for wives and children cause you to betray the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now the siege is tight, outside aid will not come, and I have divined by the Liuren method that the city will fall tomorrow. I shall die in the state's service. You too must not let thoughts of wife and children make you fail the state.

sentences.zh: 能聽吾言，當令家屬自裁，然後同赴義。」

translations.literal: If you can heed my words, have the household take their own lives, then together go to meet our righteous end."
translations.idiomatic: If you will heed me, have our families take their own lives, and then together we shall meet our righteous end."

sentences.zh: 二子泣曰：「唯吾父命。」

translations.literal: The two sons wept and said: "We obey only our father's command."
translations.idiomatic: The two sons wept and said, "We obey only our father's command."

sentences.zh: 明日，城果破，父子三人突圍力戰，死於城隅。

translations.literal: The next day the city indeed fell; the father and two sons broke out and fought with all their strength, dying at a corner of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell as he had foretold. Father and two sons broke out and fought with all their strength, and died at a corner of the wall.

sentences.zh: 孫益，不知其所以進。

translations.literal: Sun Yi—by what means he advanced is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi—by what means he rose to office is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，以福州觀察使知朔寧府，被命救太原。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, as Observation Commissioner of Fuzhou he was made prefect of Shuoning Prefecture and was ordered to rescue Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, while serving as Observation Commissioner of Fuzhou he was appointed prefect of Shuoning Prefecture and ordered to relieve Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時敵勢張甚，或言不若引兵北搗雲中，彼之將士室家在焉，所謂攻其所必救也。

translations.literal: At the time the enemy's power was very strong; some said it would be better to lead troops north to strike Yunzhong, where the enemy generals' and soldiers' families were—that is what is called attacking where they must surely come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's strength was then at its height. Some advised that he would do better to lead his troops north and strike Yunzhong, where the enemy generals' and soldiers' families lived—the classic strategy of attacking where the foe must surely come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 益曰：「此策固善，奈違君命。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "This plan is indeed good, but it goes against the sovereign's command."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "That plan is sound, but it would defy the sovereign's command."

sentences.zh: 因躍馬冒圍至城下，張孝純不肯啟門，遂死之。

translations.literal: Accordingly he leaped on a horse, burst through the encirclement to reach the foot of the wall; Zhang Xiaochun refused to open the gate, and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: He leaped onto his horse, broke through the encirclement to the foot of the wall, and died there when Zhang Xiaochun refused to open the gate.

sentences.zh: 益天資忠勇，每傾貲以賞戰士，能得人死力。

translations.literal: Yi was loyal and brave by nature; he regularly spent his own assets to reward the warriors and could win men's utmost exertion even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was loyal and brave by nature. He regularly spent his own wealth to reward his soldiers and could win their utmost devotion even unto death.

sentences.zh: 小䩴䩮為邊患，遣將致討，益子在行間，師無功，益謂子必死。

translations.literal: The Xiaorenduo caused border trouble; he dispatched a general to attack them; Yi's son was in the ranks; the army achieved nothing, and Yi said his son must die.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaorenduo raided the frontier, he dispatched a general to punish them. Yi's son marched with the army. The campaign achieved nothing, and Yi declared that his son ought to have died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，恤錄其孤甚厚。

translations.literal: The court heard of it and granted generous relief and preferment to his orphaned family.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard of this, it granted his orphaned family generous relief and honors.

sentences.zh: 其子遣信至益所報平安，益怒其子不能死，以狀自列，盡上還官所賜，而斬其持書來者。

translations.literal: His son sent a messenger to Yi's camp reporting that he was safe; Yi, angry that his son could not die, submitted a memorial stating the facts, returned all that the office had granted, and executed the man who had brought the letter.
translations.idiomatic: His son sent a messenger to Yi's camp to report that he was safe. Enraged that his son had failed to die, Yi submitted a memorial stating the facts, returned every grant the court had bestowed, and executed the man who had brought the letter.

sentences.zh: 初，益在朔寧，察郡人孫谷可用，奏為掾屬，待之異于常僚。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yi was in Shuoning, he discerned that the county man Sun Gu could be employed; he memorialized to appoint him as an aide and treated him differently from ordinary subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yi was in Shuoning, he recognized that Sun Gu, a man of the prefecture, was capable. He memorialized to appoint him as an aide and treated him with unusual favor.

sentences.zh: 益出師，屬以後事。

translations.literal: When Yi took the field, he entrusted later affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi marched out, he entrusted the affairs that would follow to Sun Gu.

sentences.zh: 益死，敵騎來攻，且別命郡守。

translations.literal: When Yi died, enemy cavalry came to attack, and at the same time a separate order was issued for a new prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, enemy cavalry came to attack, and at the same time a separate appointment was made for a new prefect.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲開關迎之，穀爭弗得，歎曰：「吾身已許國，又不忍負孫公之托，諸人不見容，是吾死所也。」

translations.literal: The crowd deliberated opening the gate to welcome them; Gu argued but could not prevail; he sighed: "My person has already been pledged to the state, and I cannot bear to fail the trust Sun Gong placed in me—since you will not tolerate me, this is where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: The men debated opening the gates to welcome the new appointee. Gu argued in vain and sighed, "I have already pledged myself to the state, and I cannot bear to betray the trust Sun Gong placed in me. Since you will not have me, this is where I shall die."

sentences.zh: 或舉刃脅之，無懾容，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Someone raised a blade to threaten him; he showed no fear, and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone raised a blade to threaten him. He showed no fear and was thereupon killed.
